AHVS 493.title: Seminar on the Williams Collection
AHVS 493.description: An intensive study of selected aspects of the Williams Collection.

AHVS 495.title: Research Workshop
AHVS 495.description: A capstone course offering advanced training in art history and visual studies. Includes a student-chosen individual research project.

ANTH 100.title: Introduction to Anthropology
ANTH 100.description: An introductory survey of the sub-fields of anthropology: biological anthropology, archaeology, cultural and social anthropology, and linguistic anthropology. Topics include the human fossil record, the archaeological record from Paleolithic cultures to urban civilizations, and examination of contemporary human societies, drawn from various levels of complexity.

ANTH 150.title: Exploring Anthropology
ANTH 150.description: Introduces topics from Anthropology on the cultural and biological diversity of past and present human and primate lives. The topic may change from year to year.

ANTH 200.title: Cultural and Social Anthropology
ANTH 200.description: Introduction to the analysis of sociocultural systems. Major topics include subsistence, production and distribution, social organization, politics, religion, kinship, symbolic systems and cultural change from an international perspective.
ANTH 200.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of the following:
    Complete all of: ANTH 100
    completed a minimum of 12 units
  or permission of the program.
requirement_notes: Alternatively: completed a minimum of 12 units
review_reasons: course requirement has a non-course alternative (completed a minimum of 12 units); courses kept as the requirement
ANTH 200.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of the following Complete all of: ANTH100 - Introduction to Anthropology (1.5) completed a minimum of 12 units or permission of the program.

ANTH 201.title: Indigenous Peoples, Colonization and Anthropology
ANTH 201.description: Provides a foundational understanding of the relationship between Indigenous Peoples and anthropology. Explores the history of colonization in Canada from an Indigenous and anthropological perspective. Examines the relationship between Indigenous Peoples and the anthropological subfields of sociocultural anthropology, archaeology, biological anthropology, linguistics and visual anthropology. Considers the historical, anthropological and ethnographic literature and how to acknowledge and move beyond the critiques.

ANTH 202.title: Food, Religion and Culture
ANTH 202.description: Investigates intersections among food, religion and culture. Addresses food prohibitions, rituals involving food, and food symbols that are present (or absent) in various religious and spiritual traditions. Pays particular attention to how religious groups and individuals use food to (1) construct relationships (real or imagined) between individuals, the community, and nonhuman beings (animals, deities, ancestors), and (2) construct and maintain cultural norms and values.

ANTH 210.title: Visual Anthropology in a Global Perspective
ANTH 210.description: Introduction to visual anthropology. Exploration of visual practice and representation through major topics including power and knowledge, visual literacy, performance, digital media, space and place, design, race, gender and sexuality.

ANTH 215.title: Money and Culture
ANTH 215.description: Explores the relationship between money and society, how money is changing, and what the implications of these changes are for economic development, poverty and inequality, and political power. Discusses what money is by analyzing the many forms it has taken, including gold, grain, shells, paper, plastic, Air Miles, computer code, and cryptocurrency. Critically reflects on contemporary money by contrasting it with examples of money from other times and cultures.

ANTH 240.title: Archaeology
ANTH 240.description: An introduction to archaeological research and problems of interpretation. Laboratories provide an opportunity to become familiar with archaeological materials and with some basic techniques of analysis.
ANTH 240.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of the following:
    Complete all of: ANTH 100
    completed a minimum of 12 units
  or permission of the program.
requirement_notes: Alternatively: completed a minimum of 12 units
review_reasons: course requirement has a non-course alternative (completed a minimum of 12 units); courses kept as the requirement
ANTH 240.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of the following Complete all of: ANTH100 - Introduction to Anthropology (1.5) completed a minimum of 12 units or permission of the program.

ANTH 241.title: Archaeology of Animals
ANTH 241.description: Examines the exceptionally long history of animal use and domestication by humans that has shaped our species and environments globally. Explores archaeological evidence for the human use of animals with a focus on food, material culture, cosmologies, economies, and social-environmental relationships. Emphasis will be on engagement with the history of global food systems and what this means for our future food security, biodiversity, and health.

ANTH 250.title: Biological Anthropology
ANTH 250.description: An introduction to human biological evolution. Topics include the study of non-human primates, investigation of the human fossil record, human skeletal variation, population genetics, growth and development and morphological variation.
ANTH 250.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of the following:
    Complete all of: ANTH 100
    completed a minimum of 12 units
  or permission of the program.
requirement_notes: Alternatively: completed a minimum of 12 units
review_reasons: course requirement has a non-course alternative (completed a minimum of 12 units); courses kept as the requirement
ANTH 250.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of the following Complete all of: ANTH100 - Introduction to Anthropology (1.5) completed a minimum of 12 units or permission of the program.

ANTH 251.title: Human Evolutionary Biology
ANTH 251.description: Examines how evolution has shaped our species through an exploration of the ways our biology reflects both our shared ancestry with other animals and our species’ unique evolutionary history, as well as what this means for our lives and our future. Emphasis is on critical engagement with evolutionary explanations for human biology, diversity, and health.

ANTH 252.title: Primates, People and Society
ANTH 252.description: Examines the special relationship that humans share with their closest living relatives, the nonhuman primates, by surveying the myriad of interactions between people and primates throughout history and in contemporary times. Emphasis will be on investigating the significance of primates for the following aspects of human societies: religion; mythology; medicine; media and global trade.

ANTH 260.title: Introduction to Anthropological Research
ANTH 260.description: Introduction to the diverse methods of inquiry and interpretation used in anthropological research, and key debates about the status of anthropological data and knowledge, the conditions of their production and innovative directions in the development of anthropological research. Focuses on the relationship between methodology and theory, ethics, research design, and qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis.
ANTH 260.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: ANTH 200, ANTH 240, ANTH 250
Pre- or corequisites:
  Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: ATWP 110, ATWP 135, ENSH 101, ENSH 102, ENSH 103
ANTH 260.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: ANTH200 - Cultural and Social Anthropology (1.5) ANTH240 - Archaeology (1.5) ANTH250 - Biological Anthropology (1.5) Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: ATWP110 - Academic Reading and Writing Support and Development (3) ATWP135 - Academic Reading and Writing (1.5) ENSH101 - Themes in Literature (1.5) ENSH102 - Literature in Action (1.5) ENSH103 - Writing, Culture, Power (1.5)

ANTH 292.title: Exploring Archaeology
ANTH 292.description: Introduces specialized topics from the subfield of archaeology.

ANTH 293.title: Exploring Cultural and Social Anthropology
ANTH 293.description: Introduces specialized topics from the subfields of cultural and social anthropology.

ANTH 294.title: Exploring Biological Anthropology
ANTH 294.description: Introduces specialized topics from the subfield of biological anthropology.

ANTH 302.title: Globalization, Health, and the Environment
ANTH 302.description: A comparative framework for understanding the relationship between global processes, the environment and health. Topics may include the origin and evolution of infectious diseases with human societies, social and economic inequalities, violence, gender, diet, health policies, technologies, pandemics, climate change, and health care industries. Emphasis on how local experiences of health are linked to global processes via the environment.

ANTH 303.title: Anthropology of Sound
ANTH 303.description: Examines sound-related dimensions from an anthropological perspective. Draws on ethnographies of listening, sound art works and recent writings in Sound Studies. Experimentation with soundscape production.

ANTH 304.title: Technology and Culture
ANTH 304.description: Critical approaches to the reciprocal relationship between technology and culture. Anthropological analysis of technological systems as sites of meaning, power and social practice. Draws on case studies from the full spectrum of human technological practices, from material culture to digital domains.

ANTH 305.title: Anthropology of the Arts
ANTH 305.description: Critical examination of theoretical and methodological approaches by anthropologists and their collaborators to the study of art, artists and their practices.

ANTH 306.title: Indigenous Storytelling Traditions
ANTH 306.description: Examines the powerful role of storytelling to pass knowledge across generations for community well-being and prosperity. Explores the chronicles of important events, experiences, and instructions that have been carefully packaged in stories by Indigenous people over multiple centuries. Engages students in deconstructing stereotypical understandings of the Indigenous storytelling and in recognizing diverse Indigenous ways of sharing a story such as song, dance, crafts, and talking circles.

ANTH 309.title: Anthropology of Film and Video
ANTH 309.description: Examination of theoretical and methodological approaches to visual anthropological research in film and video.

ANTH 311.title: Introduction to Engaged and Practicing Anthropology
ANTH 311.description: Introduction to anthropologically-informed approaches to research engaged with finding solutions to practical problems of contemporary significance. Surveys applications of anthropological research to various fields such as public policy, environment, education, law, medicine and heritage resource management. Discusses the burgeoning professional practice of anthropology outside academic institutions.

ANTH 312.title: Introduction to Medical Anthropology
ANTH 312.description: Introduction to key themes and theoretical frameworks in medical anthropology, including applied medical anthropology, cultural construction of illness and critical medical anthropology. Topics include enduring cultural traditions of healing, the place of infectious diseases in human societies, contributions and critiques of biomedicine, medicalization, nutrition, global health campaigns and the comparative study of medical systems.

ANTH 313.title: Anthropology, Food and Migration
ANTH 313.description: Explores various trends in the study of migration through the lens of food and food practices.

ANTH 314.title: Economic Anthropology
ANTH 314.description: A comparative analysis of the social context of production, distribution and exchange systems in local and global contexts.

ANTH 317.title: Quantitative Methods in Anthropological Research
ANTH 317.description: Introduces quantitative data analysis in Anthropology. Focus is on the application and interpretation of statistical techniques and information. Topics may include exploratory data analysis, parametric and nonparametric statistical tests, correlation and regression analysis, presentation of statistical information and an introduction to more specialized methods. Data analysis applications are computer based using freely available software.
ANTH 317.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: ANTH 200, ANTH 240, ANTH 250
    Complete 1 of: ANTH 260, ANTH 316
ANTH 317.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: ANTH200 - Cultural and Social Anthropology (1.5) ANTH240 - Archaeology (1.5) ANTH250 - Biological Anthropology (1.5) Complete 1 of: ANTH260 - Introduction to Anthropological Research (1.5) ANTH316 - Introduction to Anthropological Research (1.5)

ANTH 318.title: Ethnographic Research Methods
ANTH 318.description: Review of ethnographic methods used in the field by cultural anthropologists. Topics include the relationship between field methods and theory in anthropology, field experiences and techniques and qualitative data analysis.
ANTH 318.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH260 - Introduction to Anthropological Research (1.5)

ANTH 319.title: Research Methods in Archaeology and Biological Anthropology
ANTH 319.description: Research methods employed by archaeologists and biological anthropologists in lab and field settings. Topics include research design and project management, hypothesis testing, sampling, database management, data presentation, scientific writing, and the integration of new technologies to answer long-standing questions in these sub-disciplines.
ANTH 319.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: ANTH 260, ANTH 316
    Complete 1 of: ANTH 240, ANTH 250

ANTH 325.title: Anthropology of South America
ANTH 325.description: Discussion and analysis of the peoples and cultures of South America.
ANTH 325.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: ANTH 200
  or permission of the program.
ANTH 325.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH200 - Cultural and Social Anthropology (1.5) or permission of the program.

ANTH 329.title: Anthropology of Southeast Asia
ANTH 329.description: Discussion and analysis of the peoples and cultures of Mainland and Island Southeast Asia.
ANTH 329.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: ANTH 200
  or permission of the program.
ANTH 329.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH200 - Cultural and Social Anthropology (1.5) or permission of the program.

ANTH 331.title: Anthropology of Indigenous Health
ANTH 331.description: Explores Indigenous Peoples’ health in Canada through immersive and applied Indigenous practices. Focuses on anthropological understandings of culture to highlight contemporary ways that Indigenous Peoples are reclaiming and revitalizing their culture, healing, and health practices. Provides an introduction to anthropology’s role in colonization and the subsequent impacts on Indigenous Peoples’ health, focusing on the positive relationships between culture, health, language, identity, and the natural and spiritual world as a foundation for reclamation and revitalization.

ANTH 333.title: Indigenous Visions on Sustainability
ANTH 333.description: Introduces the notions of sustainability that are captured within Indigenous cultures. Examines case studies from various regions and Indigenous nations to understand epistemologies behind Indigenous visions on sustainability. Explores how these holistic systems of knowledge face environmental change and foster community well-being.

ANTH 336.title: Contemporary Themes in Indigenous Anthropology
ANTH 336.description: Survey of historical and contemporary social, political, economic and cultural issues in Indigenous communities in Canada.

ANTH 340.title: Archaeology of British Columbia
ANTH 340.description: Reviews the archaeological evidence of 14,000 years of First Nations occupation of British Columbia. Emphasizes continuity and change in subsistence, settlement, technology, and the environment from the last Ice Age through the arrival of Europeans.

ANTH 341.title: Paleolithic Archaeology
ANTH 341.description: A review of the formative phases in the development of prehistoric cultures and societies during the Plio-Pleistocene in Africa, Eurasia and Australasia. Archaeological evidence on cultural beginnings, ecology, subsistence systems, technology and social life of early humankind.

ANTH 343.title: Archaeological Field Techniques
ANTH 343.description: Training in the methods and techniques of archaeology through participation in a field project. Complements the regional topics of 344, with which it is normally combined to form the archaeological field school.
ANTH 343.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: ANTH 240
    permission of the program.
ANTH 343.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete all of: ANTH240 - Archaeology (1.5) permission of the program.

ANTH 344.title: Regional Topics in Archaeology
ANTH 344.description: Intensive study of topics in archaeological method and theory relevant to the interpretation of a single site or region. Complements the applied archaeological research of 343, with which it is normally combined to form the archaeological field school.
ANTH 344.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: ANTH 240
    permission of the program.
ANTH 344.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete all of: ANTH240 - Archaeology (1.5) permission of the program.

ANTH 346.title: Archaeology of Holocene Africa
ANTH 346.description: Explores the diverse lifeways that have characterized African societies of the last 10,000 years. Topics include the emergence of agriculture, complex societies, and the effects of global connections. Emphasizes how archaeologists approach reconstruction of the African past, and critical evaluation of archaeological interpretation.

ANTH 347.title: The Pleistocene Archaeology of Africa
ANTH 347.description: An overview of the Pleistocene archaeology Stone Age prehistory of Africa, from the earliest stone tools to the beginnings of agriculture, involving an in-depth examination of a number of important archaeological sites.

ANTH 348.title: Peopling of New Territories
ANTH 348.description: Current reconstructions show humans initially evolved in Africa and subsequently expanded their range to the extent that, by the time of European voyages of world exploration, people were already almost everywhere. Focuses on the processes by which humans discovered and adapted to previously unsettled lands. Emphasis is on archaeological data and interpretation via selected case studies, particularly the first people of Australia, the Pacific, and the Americas.

ANTH 349.title: Paleolithic Art
ANTH 349.description: Explores the evidence for the origins and development of cave art, personal adornment and symbol use in the Paleolithic and their role in the evolution of human cognition. Specific topics include the definition of art in an archeological context, dating and analysis techniques, contemporary examples of rock art, and possible meanings and functions of art and personal adornment during the Paleolithic.

ANTH 350.title: Primate Behaviour and Conservation
ANTH 350.description: Fundamentals of primate behavioural ecology, including history of the discipline within anthropology, taxonomy, sociality, ecology, behaviour, communication and conservation, including theoretical and methodological approaches for studying non-human primates.
ANTH 350.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of the following:
    Complete 1 of: ANTH 250, ANTH 251, ANTH 252, BIOL 345
    Minimum third-year standing
review_reasons: course requirement has a non-course alternative (Minimum third-year standing); courses kept as the requirement
ANTH 350.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of the following Complete 1 of: ANTH250 - Biological Anthropology (1.5) ANTH251 - Human Evolutionary Biology (1.5) ANTH252 - Primates, People and Society (1.5) BIOL345 - Animal Behaviour (1.5) Minimum third-year standing

ANTH 351.title: Human Origins
ANTH 351.description: Examines the fossil, archaeological and genetic evidence for human evolution emphasizing the interpretation and reconstruction of the human lineage.
ANTH 351.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: ANTH250 - Biological Anthropology (1.5) ANTH251 - Human Evolutionary Biology (1.5)

ANTH 352.title: Human Osteology
ANTH 352.description: Theoretical and methodological approaches to the study of human skeletal remains.
ANTH 352.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: ANTH 250, ANTH 251, BME 201
ANTH 352.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: ANTH250 - Biological Anthropology (1.5) ANTH251 - Human Evolutionary Biology (1.5) BME201 - Quantitative Human Physiology (1.5)

ANTH 357.title: Evolutionary Biology of Contemporary Health
ANTH 357.description: Introduction to human evolutionary biology. Explores how evolutionary forces have shaped human anatomy, biology and behaviour. Examines patterns of human biological variation and the genetic and environmental factors that contribute to this variation, and how biological plasticity of humans both shapes this variation and contributes to potential health problems.
ANTH 357.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: ANTH 250, ANTH 251, BIOL 184, BIOL 190B, BIOL 230, BME 201
ANTH 357.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: ANTH250 - Biological Anthropology (1.5) ANTH251 - Human Evolutionary Biology (1.5) BIOL184 - Evolution and Biodiversity (1.5) BIOL190B - General Biology II (1.5) BIOL230 - Principles of Genetics (1.5) BME201 - Quantitative Human Physiology (1.5)

ANTH 358.title: Biology of Human Skeletal Variability
ANTH 358.description: Explores the biology of variability in the modern human skeleton and the mechanisms through which skeletal diversity is shaped in our species. Main topics include the role of genetics and plasticity in shaping bone, the origins and biomechanics of bipedality, locomotor energetics, and the importance of physical activity for bone health.
ANTH 358.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: ANTH 250, ANTH 251, BIOL 184, BME 201, EPHE 141
ANTH 358.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: ANTH250 - Biological Anthropology (1.5) ANTH251 - Human Evolutionary Biology (1.5) BIOL184 - Evolution and Biodiversity (1.5) BME201 - Quantitative Human Physiology (1.5) EPHE141 - Human Anatomy (1.5)

ANTH 360.title: Zooarchaeology
ANTH 360.description: An introduction to the study of animal bones from archaeological sites, with a lecture component emphasizing general methodology and case studies from different regions and a laboratory component focusing on the analysis of Northwest Coast fauna.

ANTH 361.title: Archaeology of Medieval Europe
ANTH 361.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of medieval archaeology, illustrated through case studies and experiential learning. Explores a range of themes including status, gender, technology, religion and daily life.

ANTH 362.title: Archaeology of Children
ANTH 362.description: Drawing on data from a wide range of disciplines, explores what can be learned about the lives of children in the past and through them, the values, beliefs, and behaviours of the cultures of which they were a part.

ANTH 365.title: Colonialism and Daily Life
ANTH 365.description: Comparative analysis of how daily life was transformed through colonial processes in different regional and temporal contexts. Draws on studies in archaeology and historical anthropology from Africa, Europe, and North America to explore processes and consequences of colonial entanglements for both colonizers and the colonized. Emphasizes importance of material culture as an active component of cultural transformations.

ANTH 366.title: Anthropology of Reproduction
ANTH 366.description: A survey of contemporary anthropological research on human reproduction, including diversity in cultural meanings of childbearing and the ways in which reproduction is shaped by social hierarchies of gender, wealth, ethnicity, sexuality and disability.
ANTH 366.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH200 - Cultural and Social Anthropology (1.5)

ANTH 367.title: Heritage and Historical Archaeology Field Course
ANTH 367.description: Introduces students to the archaeological methods used in recording historical cemeteries using a hands-on approach. Students learn and practice a range of skills including data collection and management (field and lab), mapping and recording, archival research and project design and implementation.
ANTH 367.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: ANTH 240
  or permission of the department.
ANTH 367.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH240 - Archaeology (1.5) or permission of the department.

ANTH 370.title: Indigenous Languages and Cultures
ANTH 370.description: Introduces the diverse perspectives on Indigenous languages and cultures. Explores the links between languages and cultures and the issues of language shift, language ideologies, and historical trends. Examines the language policies and language revitalization practices that are implemented in various parts of the world. Seeks to understand how sustainability of these languages can be achieved.

ANTH 371.title: Anthropology of Mexico
ANTH 371.description: Introduction to the diverse peoples and cultures of Mexico from the pre-Conquest period to the present day. Topics may include colonialism, religion, narcotrafficking, neoliberalism, tourism, migration and social movements.
ANTH 371.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: ANTH 200
  or permission of the program.
ANTH 371.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH200 - Cultural and Social Anthropology (1.5) or permission of the program.

ANTH 372.title: Economic Underworlds and Globalization
ANTH 372.description: Explores the role illicit transnational flows of goods, money, information, and people play in the contemporary global economy. Topics may include borders, drugs and drug prohibition, human smuggling, organ trafficking, conflict resources and piracy.
ANTH 372.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: ANTH 200
  or permission of the program.
ANTH 372.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH200 - Cultural and Social Anthropology (1.5) or permission of the program.

ANTH 373.title: Museums and Anthropology
ANTH 373.description: Examines the roles of museums and their collections in the production of knowledge and relationships among communities of peoples. Topics may include the colonial history of museums, anthropology's role in creating collections and exhibitions, exhibition strategies, the role of museums and their collections in an era of Truth and Reconciliation, community-based research and curatorial practices. Emphasis is on engagement between Canadian museums and First Nations, Inuit and Metis communities and collections of material culture.

ANTH 380.title: Directed Experiential Learning in Anthropology
ANTH 380.description: Conducted in relation to work or volunteer activities with a host organization identified by the student and approved by the department. The student engages in experiential learning and assessment of anthropological methods in an applied setting. The student works with an instructor to identify issues to be explored and what course assessment methods will be used before the experiential learning opportunity begins. Must include at least 150 hours of work or volunteer activities. Assessment typically involves a reflective journal and final paper.

    Minimum third-year standing
    minimum GPA of 6.5 in 300- and 400-level ANTH courses
    minimum cumulative GPA of 5.5
    declared Honours or Major in Anthropology.

ANTH 381.title: Cultural Anthropology Field School Methods
ANTH 381.description: Training in the methods associated with fieldwork in cultural anthropology through participation in a field school project. Complements the regional topics of 382, with which it is normally combined to form the cultural anthropology field school.

ANTH 382.title: Cultural Anthropology Field School Regional Topics
ANTH 382.description: Immersive study of topics in cultural anthropology relevant to one or more region(s). Complements the applied cultural anthropology field methods of 381, with which it is normally combined to form the cultural anthropology field school.

ANTH 383.title: Forensic Anthropology Methods
ANTH 383.description: Introduction to the field of forensic anthropology with a focus on lab methods to: determine forensic significance, estimate time-since-death, identify and interpret trauma-related causes of death, and personal identification. Topics include the ethical treatment of human remains in a medico-legal context, the role of the forensic anthropologist in mass disaster investigation, and as an expert witness.
ANTH 383.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: ANTH 250, ANTH 251, BME 201, EPHE 141
ANTH 383.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: ANTH250 - Biological Anthropology (1.5) ANTH251 - Human Evolutionary Biology (1.5) BME201 - Quantitative Human Physiology (1.5) EPHE141 - Human Anatomy (1.5)

ANTH 384.title: Forensic Anthropology Field Course
ANTH 384.description: Outdoor field course using forensic anthropological techniques to document and excavate clandestine burials. Topics include crime-scene protocols, mapping and excavation methods, soil stratification, evidence collection, taphonomy, photography, chain of custody, and crime scene interpretation to reconstruct activities relating to a death event and body deposition for presentation in court.
ANTH 384.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: ANTH 250, ANTH 251
    Minimum third-year standing
ANTH 384.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: ANTH250 - Biological Anthropology (1.5) ANTH251 - Human Evolutionary Biology (1.5) Minimum third-year standing

ANTH 397.title: The Archaeology of Death
ANTH 397.description: Explores themes and issues in the study of mortuary practices including ethical issues, gender and identity, social organization and structure, and spirituality from the Neolithic to the early 20 th century, and in numerous cultures from various parts of the globe.

ANTH 398.title: Life and Death in the Viking World
ANTH 398.description: A detailed look at the nature and impact of the Viking expansion in the North Atlantic (including the British Isles, the Faroes, Iceland, Greenland and North America) in the period defined rather broadly from c. 800-1300 AD. The social and ecological consequences of migration are explored, drawing on a variety of sources including archaeological data, saga literature and historical sources. Misrepresentation of the Vikings in the modern world will be addressed.

ANTH 400A.title: History of Anthropological Theory
ANTH 400A.description: History and development of the major trends in anthropological theory until the mid-20th century.

    minimum fourth-year standing

ANTH 400B.title: Current Trends in Anthropological Theory
ANTH 400B.description: Survey of recent developments in anthropological theory.
ANTH 400B.requirement_summary:

ANTH 402.title: Feminist Theory and Method in Anthropology
ANTH 402.description: The history and development of feminist anthropology; contemporary debates. Emphasis on the contribution of anthropology to feminist theory and of feminist critiques to the development of anthropology.
ANTH 402.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: ANTH 200
  or permission of the program.
ANTH 402.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH200 - Cultural and Social Anthropology (1.5) or permission of the program.

ANTH 405.title: Advanced Economic Anthropology
ANTH 405.description: A seminar course that examines contemporary problems in economic anthropology and ethnographic approaches to economic action. Themes include globalization, liberalism, neoliberalism, money, finance, development, capitalism, and alternative economies.

ANTH 408.title: Anthropology and Photography
ANTH 408.description: Seminar on photography in anthropology over the late 19th century to present day. Focus on theoretical and methodological use of cameras by anthropologists for research and creative expression. Students learn methods of visual data analysis using archival photographs.
ANTH 408.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH309 - Anthropology of Film and Video (1.5)

ANTH 409.title: Applied Ethnographic Film
ANTH 409.description: Seminar-based course focused on visual research and production of ethnographic film. Production of original ethnographic videos through the use of digital cameras and computer editing software and equipment.
ANTH 409.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: ANTH 309
  or permission of the program.
ANTH 409.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH309 - Anthropology of Film and Video (1.5) or permission of the program.

ANTH 410.title: Advanced Topics in Medical Anthropology
ANTH 410.description: Examination of one or more research themes in medical anthropology.
ANTH 410.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH312 - Introduction to Medical Anthropology (1.5)

ANTH 411.title: Indigenous Arctic
ANTH 411.description: Introduction to the unique ecosystems of the Arctic, its fragile biodiversity and the rich cultures celebrated by Indigenous Peoples and local communities. Examines contemporary issues of the Circumpolar North with a primary focus on Arctic Indigenous Peoples, Arctic knowledge systems, environmental stewardship and policies. Combines course discussions, readings and assignments to enhance understanding of the place of humans in the Arctic today.

ANTH 415.title: The Anthropology of Money in Theory and Practice
ANTH 415.description: Through experiential learning, engages in anthropological and archival research methods, examines current theory in economic anthropology and the anthropology of money, and explores how to use theoretical analysis to better understand empirical data.

ANTH 427.title: Graphic Anthropology
ANTH 427.description: Drawing and sketching as a mode of inquiry to engage and record social worlds and natural environments. Hands-on learning through development of observational skills using creative research methods and techniques for visual research expression. Exploration of past and present use of drawing in fieldnotes and sketchbooks by anthropologists and archaeologists, research illustration and publications such as comics, zines and graphic novels.

ANTH 433.title: Ethnographic Approaches to Coast Salish Land, Law and Culture
ANTH 433.description: Explores, through ethnography and Indigenous narratives, connections between land, law and culture for contemporary and historical Coast Salish communities and their implications for Indigenous rights, title and governance.
ANTH 433.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: ANTH 200, IS 201
    Minimum third-year standing
ANTH 433.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: ANTH200 - Cultural and Social Anthropology (1.5) IS201 - Introduction to Indigenous Studies (1.5) Minimum third-year standing

ANTH 436.title: Applied Indigenous Ways of Knowing
ANTH 436.description: Explores Indigenous ontology, epistemology, and pedagogy through an applied process of learning.

ANTH 441.title: Archaeological Theory
ANTH 441.description: In-depth exploration of the theoretical foundations of the discipline with an emphasis on points of conflict and consensus in archaeology today; ethical issues of archaeological practice are also addressed.

ANTH 442.title: Marine Historical Ecology
ANTH 442.description: Seminar on the role of archaeological information in contemporary ocean management and conservation via the interdisciplinary framework of marine historical ecology. Examines anthropological and ecological theory and datasets from the worlds’ oceans, islands, and coastlines, including information from communities, museums, and archives. Highlights the analytical potential of ecological data obtained from coastal archaeological sites.
ANTH 442.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: ANTH 240, ES 240
    Minimum third-year standing.
ANTH 442.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: ANTH240 - Archaeology (1.5) ES240 - Ecological Processes (1.5) Minimum third-year standing.

ANTH 449.title: Archaeology of the Northwest Coast
ANTH 449.description: Study of problems of interpreting Northwest Coast archaeological data. Field trips are scheduled.

ANTH 450.title: Seminar in Primate Cognition and Behaviour
ANTH 450.description: Seminar course focused on in-depth exploration of topics related to primate behavioural ecology such as feeding ecology, socio-ecology, reproductive ecology, communication, tool use, conservation, non-human primate cultures, and methodologies and theoretical approaches within the field. Multi-species comparative approaches are used.
ANTH 450.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of the following:
    Complete all of: ANTH 350
    Permission of the program
ANTH 450.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of the following Complete all of: ANTH350 - Primate Behaviour and Conservation (1.5) Permission of the program

ANTH 452.title: Advanced Topics in Human Osteology
ANTH 452.description: Detailed examination of topics relating to the analysis of human skeletal remains. Topics may include: skeletal biology, evolutionary anatomy and forensic osteology.
ANTH 452.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ANTH352 - Human Osteology (1.5)

ANTH 454.title: Approaches to Human Bioarchaeology
ANTH 454.description: A seminar course that examines the methodological, theoretical and ethical issues involved in the study of human skeletal remains from archaeological contexts to reconstruct life histories of past populations and individuals.
ANTH 454.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: ANTH 240, ANTH 250, ANTH 251, BME 201
    Minimum third-year standing
ANTH 454.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: ANTH240 - Archaeology (1.5) ANTH250 - Biological Anthropology (1.5) ANTH251 - Human Evolutionary Biology (1.5) BME201 - Quantitative Human Physiology (1.5) Minimum third-year standing

ANTH 456.title: Evolutionary Anthropology
ANTH 456.description: Explores evolutionary theory as applied to anthropological questions relevant to humans and non-human primates. Examines how foundational concepts and thinkers in Evolutionary Theory have shaped scientific and popular perceptions about humans and how evolutionary anthropologists are critically re-evaluating these models and their historical biases.
ANTH 456.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:

ANTH 460.title: Ethnographic Mapping and Indigenous Cartographies
ANTH 460.description: Skills-based seminar on land use and occupancy mapping (also called Traditional Use Study mapping) of indigenous territories in respect of land claims and resource rights, and critically evaluating power relations, knowledge practices, and ontologies of 'counter-mapping' and other contemporary indigenous cartographies.

ART 100E.title: Studio Foundation
ART 100E.description: The processes and ideas associated with contemporary art. Students explore a range of studio practices and theoretical issues.

ART 101E.title: Drawing
ART 101E.description: An introduction to concerns and methods in contemporary drawing. Students gain experience in a range of studio practices as well as theoretical issues through projects and critiques.
ART 101E.requirement_summary:
Pre- or corequisites:
  Completed or concurrently enrolled in all of: ART 100E
ART 101E.prerequisite_text: Completed or concurrently enrolled in all of: ART100E - Studio Foundation (1.5)

ART 103.title: Foundation Drawing and Painting
ART 103.description: One of four courses forming the foundation year for studies in Visual Arts, this course is divided into two modules. The drawing module introduces the methods, materials and concerns in contemporary drawing through studio exercises and projects. The painting module introduces contemporary painting through studio projects exploring fundamental elements, materials and concepts.

ART 104.title: Foundation Sculpture and Material Methods
ART 104.description: One of four courses forming the foundation year for studies in Visual Arts, this course focuses on the processes and ideas associated with material technologies in the visual arts and with the practices of contemporary sculpture. Students explore a range of workshop and studio practices and theoretical issues.

ART 105.title: Foundation Photography and Video Art
ART 105.description: One of four courses forming the foundation year for studies in Visual Arts. Focuses on the processes and ideas associated with the practices of contemporary photography and video art. Students explore a range of studio practices and theoretical issues.

ART 105E.title: Foundation Photography and Video Art
ART 105E.description: Focuses on the processes and ideas associated with the practices of contemporary digital photography and video art from an Indigenous perspective. Explores a range of studio practices and theoretical issues.

ART 106.title: Foundation Core Media Technologies and Arts
ART 106.description: One of four courses forming the foundation year for studies in Visual Arts, this course focuses on the core digital technologies applicable to the visual arts.

ART 106E.title: Foundation Core Media Technologies and Arts
ART 106E.description: Focuses on the core digital technologies applicable to the visual and literary arts from an Indigenous perspective.

ART 115.title: Exploring Drawing and Colour
ART 115.description: Experiential introduction to a wide range of traditional and contemporary aspects of drawing and colour in two-dimensional form. Explores materials, techniques, practices, theoretical issues and the development of drawing and colour in Visual Art.

ART 116.title: An Introduction to Documentary Photography
ART 116.description: An introductory lecture and experiential course focusing on the practice and ideas associated with documentary photography. Students gain insight and experience in documentary photography as a practice.

ART 117.title: An Introduction to Observational Drawing
ART 117.description: An introductory lecture and experiential course focusing on the practice and ideas associated with observational drawing. Students gain insight and experience into observational drawing as a practice.

ART 118.title: An Introduction to Colour
ART 118.description: An introduction to a wide range of traditional and contemporary aspects of colour including hue, lightness and chroma, brightness and saturation and visual perception of colour. Through projects and exercises students gain insight into colour mixing and the visual effects of colour combinations through projects and exercises.

ART 130E.title: Printmaking
ART 130E.description: An introductory course in printmaking techniques which prepares the student for more advanced printmaking courses.
ART 130E.requirement_summary:
Pre- or corequisites:
  Completed or concurrently enrolled in all of: ART 100E, ART 101E
ART 130E.prerequisite_text: Completed or concurrently enrolled in all of: ART100E - Studio Foundation (1.5) ART101E - Drawing (1.5)

ART 141.title: An Introduction to Contemporary Art Photography
ART 141.description: An introductory lecture and practical course focusing on the ideas associated with contemporary art photography. Through lectures introducing students to various practices of contemporary photographers and photography assignments, students gain insight into photography as an art practice within the field of contemporary art.

ART 150E.title: Introduction to Contemporary Art Theory, Criticism and Practice
ART 150E.description: Introduces the terms and concepts necessary for an understanding of contemporary art from an Indigenous perspective.

ART 155.title: Introduction to Contemporary Art Practices
ART 155.description: Introduces a historical and conceptual framework for creating, observing, and discussing contemporary art. Features presentations by living artists to explore connections between historical practices and contemporary approaches.

ART 156.title: Themes in Contemporary Art Practice
ART 156.description: Explores contemporary art through a thematic, non-linear approach, framing concepts and ideas for creating, observing, and discussing art. Draws on presentations by living artists to examine thematic associations in artistic practice.

ART 201.title: Drawing
ART 201.description: An introduction to concerns and methods in contemporary drawing. Students gain experience in a range of studio practices as well as theoretical issues through projects and critiques.
ART 201.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: ART 100, ART 100E, ART 103
ART 201.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: ART100 - Studio Foundation (1.5) ART100E - Studio Foundation (1.5) ART103 - Foundation Drawing and Painting (1.5)

ASL 100A.title: American Sign Language I
ASL 100A.description: Introduction to language used by the Deaf community in North America; no prior knowledge required. Covers essentials of grammar, basic vocabulary and fundamental structures for everyday interaction; provides insight into the Deaf community and Deaf culture.

ASL 100B.title: American Sign Language II
ASL 100B.description: Emphasis on increasing vocabulary, skills applying grammatical features, facial expression and receptive and expressive signing.
ASL 100B.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ASL100A - American Sign Language I (1.5)

ASL 200A.title: American Sign Language III
ASL 200A.description: Providing essentials of fundamental structures for everyday interaction. Develops appropriate grammatical features and facial grammar including non-manual signals in addition to receptive and expressive signing skills. Presents insight into the Deaf community and Deaf Culture.
ASL 200A.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ASL100B - American Sign Language II (1.5)

ASL 200B.title: American Sign Language IV
ASL 200B.description: Develops vocabulary and appropriate signing registers as well as skills for role-shifting and point of view when narrating in sign language, including the use of three-dimensional space and placement. Builds knowledge and understanding of Deaf culture.
ASL 200B.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ASL200A - American Sign Language III (1.5)

ASL 300A.title: American Sign Language V
ASL 300A.description: Intermediate-level ASL. Develops skills in communicating complex concepts using appropriate grammatical structures. Emphasizes the use of directionality, placement and three-dimensional space in conjunction with role-shifting and the refinement of expressive and receptive skills. Continues to expand the knowledge and understanding of Deaf culture.
ASL 300A.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ASL200B - American Sign Language IV (1.5)

ASL 300B.title: American Sign Language VI
ASL 300B.description: Focus on the production of classifiers, other complex grammatical structures and non-manual signals with an aim to achieve fluidity and fluency in narration. Practice in both formal and informal registers. Includes cross-cultural discussions of issues facing the Deaf community and non-Deaf signers.
ASL 300B.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ASL300A - American Sign Language V (1.5)

ASTR 101.title: Exploring the Night Sky
ASTR 101.description: A general course designed for non-science students. A tour of the solar system: the nature and origins of planets and moons, comets, asteroids, and the sun. Discoveries of recent space exploration and the history of our changing views of our place in the universe. Eclipses, seasons, climatic cycles, dangers posed by meteorite impacts. The possibility of extraterrestrial life. Practical work includes observations with campus telescopes.

ASTR 102.title: Exploring the Cosmos
ASTR 102.description: A general course designed for non-science students. An exploration of how astronomical observations guide and challenge our understanding of the fundamental laws of nature. Cosmology, and the elusive dark matter and dark energy that determine the universe's fate. Stars, galaxies, and relics left over by the Big Bang. Black holes and relativity; supernovae and neutron stars. Practical work includes observations with campus telescopes.

ASTR 150.title: Concepts in Modern Astronomy
ASTR 150.description: Introduces some of the great ideas and concepts in modern astronomy, as well as the basic physical principles required to understand these concepts. Topics include properties of the solar system, extrasolar planets, galaxies, expanding universe, big bang, origin of the elements, dark matter, dark energy, black holes, neutron stars.

ASTR 201.title: The Search for Life in the Universe
ASTR 201.description: A general science course designed to be accessible to students not majoring in science. An overview of modern scientific thought on the possibility of life beyond Earth and the current research being done to find it; the likeliest locations of life in our Solar System; the hunt for planets around other stars; the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI). Laboratories on alternate weeks; practical work includes observations with campus telescopes.

ASTR 250.title: Introduction to Astrophysics
ASTR 250.description: Provides the physical foundation and introduction of astronomical terminology that is used in subsequent courses. Topics include astronomical coordinate systems, telescopes, stellar distances and magnitudes, binary stars, spectral classification, stellar evolution, variable stars, stellar motions, star clusters, interstellar medium, structure and rotation of the galaxy, external galaxies.

ASTR 303.title: Introductory Extragalactic Astronomy
ASTR 303.description: Kinematics and morphology of spiral (including the Milky Way), elliptical and irregular galaxies. Introduction to current theory for the formation and evolution of galaxies and the large-scale structure. Observations of active galactic nuclei, jets and quasi-stellar objects.

ASTR 304.description: Astronomy and astrophysics of planets and planetary systems. The Solar System and extrasolar planetary systems. Planet formation, orbits, measurements of the properties of planets, detection, study of extrasolar planets, and the Earth-Moon system.

ASTR 480.description: Occasional offerings dealing with a specific topic in Astronomy.

ATWP 100A.title: English Language for Academic Success
ATWP 100A.description: English Language Centre course for English language learners. Honing of skills necessary to communicate in English in writing and oral presentations at the university level. Readings feature complex structures and a wide range of topics. Assignments use foundational research skills, documentation conventions and rhetorical styles.

ATWP 100B.title: Advanced English Language for Academic Success
ATWP 100B.description: English Language Centre course for English language learners. Honing of skills necessary to write multi-paragraph, stylistically complex texts in English in a variety of rhetorical styles. Instruction in writing processes. Assignments include a coherent research essay.

ATWP 101.title: Fundamentals of Academic Literacy
ATWP 101.description: Introduction to the reading and writing skills needed to meet the expectations of university-level academic study. Emphasis is on building proficiency in academic reading and writing through extensive practice. Suitable for students who need to strengthen their reading and writing skills before attempting a course that meets the Academic Writing Requirement.

ATWP 110.title: Academic Reading and Writing Support and Development
ATWP 110.description: Introduces foundational English reading and writing skills; structured practice of advanced skills needed for advanced academic writing; balance of lectures, discussions, and paired or group work.

ATWP 135.title: Academic Reading and Writing
ATWP 135.description: Practice of skills needed for successful academic writing in a variety of subject areas. Analysis of rhetorical, stylistic, research and documentation techniques; development of these techniques through practical writing assignments. Balance of lectures and discussion.

ATWP 250.title: Genres of Business Communication
ATWP 250.description: Introduces conventional business communication genres, such as proposals, recommendation reports, letters, memos and email. Focus on writing for multiple audiences across varied cultural and organizational contexts. Emphasis on skills in business communication including collaborative writing, self-assessment, writing to inform, writing to persuade and professional standards.

    Complete 1.5 units of: an AWR-designated course
    or permission of the department.

Alternatively: or permission of the department.

ATWP 305.title: Language and Rhetoric in Health and Medicine
ATWP 305.description: Explores how language creates, establishes and sometimes settles controversies in health and medicine. Examines how health communication impacts medical care and how language shapes health communication and outcomes. Includes politicians' use of military metaphors during pandemics, patients’ experiences of illnesses unrecognized by medical professionals, the role of social media in creating and resisting vaccine hesitancy, the history of medical racism as justified by scientific “objectivity” and the impact of pharmaceutical marketing on self-diagnosis.

BEM 300.title: Biomedical Regulatory Affairs
BEM 300.description: Regulatory frameworks for medical devices, pharmaceuticals, and healthcare products. FDA, EMA, and other global regulations, compliance strategies and the approval process. Regulatory compliance and bringing innovations to market.

BEM 310.title: Digital Health
BEM 310.description: Fundamentals of digital health, emerging technologies, data analytics, ethical considerations.

BEM 311.title: Wearable Technology
BEM 311.description: Design, development and applications of wearable devices for health monitoring, diagnostics and treatment. Principles and challenges associated with wearable devices, projects and case studies.

BEM 312.title: Telemedicine and Remote Patient Monitoring
BEM 312.description: Applications including video conferencing, remote diagnostics, home health monitoring. Benefits and challenges of telemedicine, regulatory and ethical considerations.

BEM 315.title: Healthcare Development Management
BEM 315.description: Healthcare development applied to healthcare decision-making and management. Economic evaluation methods, healthcare financing, cost-benefit analysis. The systemic inequities that affect Indigenous populations, including barriers to healthcare access, the underrepresentation of Indigenous voices in healthcare decision-making and the economic challenges of providing equitable care to communities.

BEM 317.title: Technology Commercialization
BEM 317.description: Regulatory compliance, intellectual property management, market analysis. Strategies for bringing new technologies to market, managing IP portfolios, navigating regulatory landscapes, commercialization pathways.

BEM 412.title: Health Data Analytics
BEM 412.description: Collection, analysis, and interpretation of health data using statistical and computational methods. Data mining techniques, machine learning algorithms, visualization tools, extracting insights from health data for improving patient care, research and healthcare administration.

BEM 415.title: Internet of Medical Things (IoMT)
BEM 415.description: Integration of medical devices into the Internet of Things (IoT). Applications of IoMT in healthcare, including data security, interoperability, and the use of IoT devices for remote monitoring, patient care, and research.

BEM 416.title: Clinical Engineering
BEM 416.description: Engineering principles applied to healthcare: design; maintenance; safety regulations; healthcare technology assessment; sustainable life-cycle assessment.

BEM 418.title: Clinical Trials and Research Methodologies
BEM 418.description: Designing and conducting clinical trials. Methodologies, ethical considerations, data analysis, regulatory requirements. Practical insights into trial management. Applying research findings to improve patient outcomes.

BEM 430.title: Project Management Biomedical Devices and Digital Health
BEM 430.description: Integrates biomedical knowledge and skills to address real challenges in healthcare and medical technology. Conception, design, validating, costing, project management and marketing plan for a biomedical device or system. Interdisciplinary collaboration, critical thinking, innovation and effective communication.

BIOC 299.title: Biochemistry for Non-Majors
BIOC 299.description: An introduction to the concepts of biochemistry intended for students not majoring in biochemistry or microbiology. Properties of bio-molecules, basic enzymology and metabolism. Bioenergetics, nucleic acid structure and synthesis. Protein synthesis. Structure and properties of membranes.
BIOC 299.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CHEM231 - Introduction to Organic Chemistry (1.5)

BIOC 300A.title: General Biochemistry I
BIOC 300A.description: BIOC 300A and 300B are intended to provide detailed coverage of foundation topics for students majoring in biochemistry or microbiology and must be taken sequentially. Protein structure and function, enzymes and enzyme kinetics, carbohydrates, lipids, biological membranes and bioenergetics.
BIOC 300A.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 225, BME 200
    Complete all of: CHEM 231

BIOC 300B.title: General Biochemistry II
BIOC 300B.description: BIOC 300A and 300B are intended to provide detailed coverage of foundation topics for students majoring in biochemistry or microbiology. Metabolic processes and their control, as well as structure and function of DNA, RNA and genes.
BIOC 300B.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: BIOC 300A, BIOL 225, CHEM 231
    Complete 1 of: CHEM 232, CHEM 234, CHEM 235

BIOC 401.title: RNA in Health and Disease
BIOC 401.description: Advanced study of RNA biology in eukaryotes, including RNA synthesis regulation from both single gene and genomic perspectives; RNA processing; and the functions of non-coding RNAs. Emphasis is on recent breakthroughs in RNA biology and the mechanisms driving development and human disease.
BIOC 401.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOC 300A, BIOC 300B
BIOC 401.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOC300A - General Biochemistry I (1.5) BIOC300B - General Biochemistry II (1.5)

BIOC 403.title: Disrupted Cell Signaling in Human Disease
BIOC 403.description: Advanced study of biochemical basis of molecular signal transmission from a cell's exterior to its interior to bring about changes in cellular behaviour and gene expression. Focus is on how cellular signalling is disrupted in human disease and how therapeutics are developed.
BIOC 403.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOC 300A, BIOC 300B
BIOC 403.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOC300A - General Biochemistry I (1.5) BIOC300B - General Biochemistry II (1.5)

BIOC 404.title: Protein Structure and Molecular Interactions
BIOC 404.description: Detailed examination of protein structure and function emphasizing techniques for the determination of protein structure and the study of protein interactions in binding and catalysis.
BIOC 404.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOC 300A, BIOC 300B
BIOC 404.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOC300A - General Biochemistry I (1.5) BIOC300B - General Biochemistry II (1.5)

BIOC 408.title: Epigenetics and Genome Dynamics
BIOC 408.description: Chemical modifications of the chromatin fibre including chromatin organization, histone post-translational modifications, histone variants, and DNA methylation. A special emphasis on epigenetics in gene regulation and nuclear metabolism with a discussion of current literature highlighting the role of epigenetics in human disease.
BIOC 408.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOC 300A, BIOC 300B
BIOC 408.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOC300A - General Biochemistry I (1.5) BIOC300B - General Biochemistry II (1.5)

BIOC 409.title: Mass Spectrometry in the Life Sciences
BIOC 409.description: Introduction to mass spectrometry for biological applications. Includes review of mass analyzers and ionization methods; analytical strategies for the detection, characterization and quantification of proteins and metabolites; use of tandem mass spectrometry to determine protein sequence and metabolite structure; identification and localization of protein post-translational modifications; application of proteomics methods to drug development, clinical screening and characterizing molecular interactions; introductory informatics; and use of metabolomics and proteomics in health research.
BIOC 409.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOC 300A, BIOC 300B
BIOC 409.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOC300A - General Biochemistry I (1.5) BIOC300B - General Biochemistry II (1.5)

BIOL 150A.title: Modern Biology
BIOL 150A.description: An introduction to biological science, emphasizing the diversity of living organisms and the evolutionary and ecological principles underlying this diversity. Topics include the history of life on earth, mechanisms of evolution, and the ecology of populations, communities and ecosystems (including human ecology).

BIOL 150B.title: Modern Biology
BIOL 150B.description: An introduction to biological science, emphasizing cellular and physiological processes. Topics include principles of genetics, cell biology, plant physiology and animal physiology.

BIOL 184.title: Evolution and Biodiversity
BIOL 184.description: An introductory course in the biological sciences. Evolutionary theory, Mendelian genetics, mitosis and the cell cycle, meiosis and sexual life cycles, and diversity of prokaryotes, protists, plants, fungi, invertebrates and craniates.
BIOL 184.requirement_summary:

    Biology 12

BIOL 186.title: Physiology and Cell Biology
BIOL 186.description: An introductory course in the biological sciences. Biological chemistry, cellular diversity, membrane structure and function, energy transduction, DNA replication. Structure, growth, nutrition, and development of plants; principles of animal physiology including homeostatic mechanisms, circulation, gas exchange, osmoregulation, thermoregulation, defense systems, chemical signalling, reproduction and development.
BIOL 186.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of the following:

BIOL 215.title: Principles of Ecology
BIOL 215.description: An introduction to factors controlling the distribution and abundance of plants and animals. Physical environments of organisms; biotic environments and interactions among species; factors influencing population growth; behavioural ecology; community ecology; succession; trophic levels and energy flow, island biogeography; biodiversity; human impact on global ecology; conservation ecology.
BIOL 215.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 184, BIOL 190B
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 186, BIOL 190A
  or permission of the department.

BIOL 225.title: Principles of Cell Biology
BIOL 225.description: An introduction to cellular, subcellular, and molecular structure/function relationships in eukaryotic cells. Membrane structure and dynamics, membrane transport, protein sorting, vesicular transport, endocytic pathways, extracellular matrices, interactions with the cellular and acellular environments, endomembrane system, cytoskeleton and motility, cellular reproduction, mechanisms of cell signalling, techniques in cell biology.
BIOL 225.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: BIOL 186, BIOL 190A
  or permission of the department.

BIOL 230.title: Principles of Genetics
BIOL 230.description: Introduction to principles of inheritance. Classical genetic theory; meiosis, mitosis, recombination, population genetics and evolution, genotype, phenotype, random assortment, dominance, DNA structure, function, replication and molecular basis of inheritance. RNA and protein synthesis, regulation of transcription and gene organization. Introduction to DNA technologies.

Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOL 225
Pre- or corequisites:
  Completed or concurrently enrolled in all of: CHEM 231

BIOL 248.title: Topics in Organismal Biology
BIOL 248.description: Special topics demonstrating how the functioning of whole organisms can be understood by integrating multiple levels of biological organization. Includes topics dealing with both plants and animals.
BIOL 248.requirement_summary:

    Complete 1 of: BIOL 184, BIOL 190B, MICR 200A

BIOL 307.title: Chordate Zoology
BIOL 307.description: Chordates: evolutionary history and adaptations. Major taxonomic groups, with emphasis on derived and defining characteristics; locomotion, feeding, sensory systems and reproduction. Laboratory exercises include observations of prepared specimens, dissections, written assignments and oral presentations.
BIOL 307.requirement_summary:

  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 184, BIOL 190B
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 186, BIOL 190A

BIOL 309.title: Developmental Biology
BIOL 309.description: Cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying animal development: fertilization, gastrulation, body axis formation and patterning, formation of the eye, nervous system, neural crest, limb, germ cells and gonads. Emphasis on human developmental disorders, experimental design and hypothesis testing. Laboratory is divided into wet labs (model organisms and embryological techniques) and dry labs (analysis of primary literature).

BIOL 311.title: Biological Oceanography
BIOL 311.description: An introduction to the ways in which physical, chemical and biological processes interact to regulate structure and productivity of marine ecosystems. Lectures focus primarily on planktonic ecosystems. Participation in a one-day oceanographic cruise is required.

BIOL 312.title: Entomology
BIOL 312.description: The study of insects, focusing on phylogenetics, ecology and evolution. Topics include: medical entomology, plant-insect interactions, and social insects. The lab focuses on insect identification and collecting techniques.

BIOL 319.title: Marine Ecology
BIOL 319.description: The agents that control the distribution of organisms and structure of marine communities, including the influence of environmental conditions on plant and animal populations, organic matter and nutrient cycling, consumer dynamics and competition, community stability and diversity.

BIOL 321.title: Survey of Invertebrates
BIOL 321.description: Invertebrate diversity in an evolutionary perspective. Morphology, life histories, phylogeny and upper level systematics; selected aspects of behaviour and physiology. Laboratory exercises include study of live and preserved specimens.
BIOL 321.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 186, BIOL 190A
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 184, BIOL 190B
    Complete all of: BIOL 225

BIOL 322.title: Biology of Marine Invertebrates
BIOL 322.description: Selected functional categories of invertebrate adaptations. In particular: defensive adaptations, adaptations related to feeding and nutrition, symbiotic relationships, musculo-skeletal systems and reproductive and developmental adaptations. Emphasis is on interpretation of data from the published literature. Laboratory exercises involve study of live material and include observations on behaviour, larval types, and anatomy as exposed by dissections.
BIOL 322.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOL321 - Survey of Invertebrates (1.5)

BIOL 324.title: Biology of Land Plants
BIOL 324.description: Plant diversity in an evolutionary perspective. Anatomy, morphology, phylogeny and ecology of bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms. Laboratories emphasize local plants and include field trips.
BIOL 324.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 184, BIOL 190B
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 186, BIOL 190A

BIOL 325.title: Tree Biology
BIOL 325.description: The unique features and specialized adaptations of trees. Tree physiology, cell biology, morphology and anatomy. Laboratory exercises and field trips reinforce lecture concepts.
BIOL 325.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Earn a minimum grade of B in each of the following: BIOL 225
BIOL 325.prerequisite_text: Earn a minimum grade of B in each of the following: BIOL225 - Principles of Cell Biology (1.5)

BIOL 326.title: Development and Genetics of Model Plants
BIOL 326.description: The genetic basis of anatomy, development, physiology and ecology in model plants such as poplar and Arabidopsis. Labs emphasize phenotypic and genetic analysis of plant mutants.
BIOL 326.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOL 215, BIOL 225, BIOL 230
BIOL 326.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOL215 - Principles of Ecology (1.5) BIOL225 - Principles of Cell Biology (1.5) BIOL230 - Principles of Genetics (1.5)

BIOL 329.title: Biology of the Vertebrates of British Columbia
BIOL 329.description: Factors that influence the organization, distribution and diversity of vertebrates in BC. Topics include: natural history, systematics, sample design, biodiversity and conservation initiatives. Course goals are to appreciate the diversity of vertebrates and understand life histories and species-at-risk issues. The lab focuses on identification of over 400 species of vertebrates by using calls, digital images, and study skins. Optional field trips. Attendance at the Annual Vertebrate Symposium is mandatory.
BIOL 329.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: BIOL 215
    minimum third-year standing.

BIOL 330.title: Study Design and Data Analysis
BIOL 330.description: An introduction to the statistical analysis of biological data, experimental design and sampling design. Laboratories emphasize computer-based analysis of biological data.

BIOL 334.title: Plants and People
BIOL 334.description: Plants as sources of food, fibre, drugs, and industrial raw materials from historical and contemporary perspectives. Aspects of plant growth, development, physiology, genetics and pathology, particularly as they relate to the economic uses of plants.

BIOL 335.title: Ichthyology
BIOL 335.description: The evolution and diversity of fishes. Emphasis on form and function, ecology, behaviour, sensory modes, fishery management, global crises in fisheries, and marine protected areas. Laboratories include identification of major groups of fishes, methodology and experimental approaches to the study of fishes.
BIOL 335.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: BIOL 215
    minimum third-year standing.
BIOL 335.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete all of: BIOL215 - Principles of Ecology (1.5) minimum third-year standing.

BIOL 336.title: Biology of Algae
BIOL 336.description: A survey of aquatic and terrestrial algal diversity, with special emphasis on marine algae. Evolution, ecology, physiology, cell biology, and technological applications of algae. Laboratories include observations of microscopic and macroscopic algal specimens, an individual project, and local field trips to coastal marine environments.
BIOL 336.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOL 215, BIOL 225
BIOL 336.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOL215 - Principles of Ecology (1.5) BIOL225 - Principles of Cell Biology (1.5)

BIOL 345.title: Animal Behaviour
BIOL 345.description: Evolutionary and comparative analyses of animal behaviour. Topics include foraging behaviours, evolution of sex, mate choice, sociality, empathy, conflict and play, nature/nurture controversies, sensory modalities, communication and the evolution of language, hemispheric dominance and laterality, taxonomic diversity of nervous systems, proximate and ultimate mechanisms for interpreting behaviour. Laboratory includes observational and experimental approaches to behaviour of representative invertebrate and vertebrate taxa and a field research project.

BIOL 346.title: Freshwater Ecosystems
BIOL 346.description: Provides a basic understanding of the geological, physical, chemical, and biological processes that form and maintain lake and reservoir ecosystems. Covers both theoretical and applied aspects of freshwater ecology, and discusses the studies and experiments that have been used to test important theories and applications. Also covers anthropogenic and environmental threats to and impacts on freshwater ecosystems.

  Complete 1 of: BIOL 215, ES 240, GEOG 272

BIOL 351.title: The Biology behind the News
BIOL 351.description: An examination of the biological science that bears on current environmental, social, ethical and political issues. Emphasis on how an understanding of the science might inform decision-making by individuals and groups.

BIOL 355.title: Evolution
BIOL 355.description: Evolutionary processes and the spatial and temporal patterns they produce. Natural selection, genetic drift and other microevolutionary processes; the basis of morphological and molecular change; species and speciation; macroevolution; phylogeny reconstruction; origin of life.
BIOL 355.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOL230 - Principles of Genetics (1.5)

BIOL 359.title: Food, Disease and People
BIOL 359.description: Microorganisms and their role in human societies today and in the past. Microorganisms in fermentation of food (cheese, sourdough bread) and beverages (wine, beer) but also in foodborne and non-foodborne diseases (listeriosis, plague). Aspects of growth, genetics, evolution and ecology of microorganisms as part of food and diseases with an emphasis on bacteria and their classification. Importance of microorganisms in trade and history.

BIOL 360.title: Cell Biology
BIOL 360.description: Structure and function of animal and plant cells and tissues, membrane structure, transport, cellular compartments, cytoskeleton, cell growth and division, cell adhesion, extracellular matrix, tissue organization and renewal.

BIOL 361.title: Molecular Genetics and Genomics
BIOL 361.description: Naturally occurring and induced genetic mutations leading to phenotypic variation within and among species in a diversity of eukaryotic taxa. Regulation of transcription and translation (including small regulatory RNAs), protein-protein interactions, molecular mechanisms of tumor formation, genome structure and mobile genetic elements, and functional genomics.

BIOL 362.title: Practical Skills in Genomics
BIOL 362.description: An introduction to advanced experimental techniques in molecular biology and genomics. Course includes nucleic acid (DNA) isolation, polymerase chain reaction (PCR), DNA quality control, next generation DNA sequencing, computer-based analysis of large scale nucleotide sequence data such as DNA sequence assembly and mapping, BLAST searches, multiple sequence alignment, taxonomic assignment, and phylogenetic analyses. Student-collected data from one or more lab projects will be used to develop skills in contemporary genomics research and in scientific manuscript writing.

BIOL 365.title: Animal Physiology
BIOL 365.description: Fundamentals of animal physiological systems: principles of cellular and organismic homeostasis, nutrition, digestion, salt/water balance, respiration, circulation, muscle contraction, excitable membranes, sensory systems, brain functions, hormones, reproduction. Laboratory includes study of live animals.

BIOL 366.title: Plant Physiology
BIOL 366.description: Principles of plant physiology: photosynthesis, water relations, ion uptake, translocation, carbohydrates, nitrogen and lipid metabolism, phenolics, phytohormones, tropisms, phytochromes.
BIOL 366.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOL 225

BIOL 367.title: Neurobiology: Molecules to Behaviour
BIOL 367.description: Cellular and molecular biology of excitable cells and mechanisms of intercellular communication. Evolution and functional organization of central nervous systems. Motor systems and mechanisms of coordination. Sensory biology. Interactions of genes, development, and experience in molding nervous systems and behaviour.
BIOL 367.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: BIOL 360, BIOL 365, BME 200, BME 201

BIOL 370.title: Conservation Biology
BIOL 370.description: Diversity of organisms, functioning of ecosystems, and the impact of human activities on these. Topics include the nature of biological diversity; extinction and its cause; habitat alteration and fragmentation; effects of exotic species; economic and ethical considerations; practical applications and analytical tools; and legal frameworks for conserving species and habitats.
BIOL 370.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 186, BIOL 190A
    Complete all of: BIOL 215, BIOL 230
    Complete 1 of: STAT 255, STAT 260
