BIOL 388.title: Applied Molecular Biology
BIOL 388.description: Applications of molecular biology in a range of fields such as forensics, genetic counselling, environmental DNA (eDNA), large-scale industrial drug and protein production.
BIOL 388.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOL230 - Principles of Genetics (1.5)

BIOL 400.title: History of Biology
BIOL 400.description: The historical development of the major techniques and ideas of biology, including the significance of the important historical contributors to biology.

BIOL 401A.title: Biotechnology
BIOL 401A.description: The tools of molecular biology and biotechnology (including the enzymes, cloning vectors and cloning strategies used in recombinant DNA technology, as well as the origins of these tools), and the application of genetic engineering to medicine, agriculture, forestry, forensic science and related areas. Lectures also include bioethics and the impact of biotechnology on society.
BIOL 401A.requirement_summary:
Pre- or corequisites:
  Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: BIOL 360, BIOL 361, BIOC 300B
BIOL 401A.prerequisite_text: Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: BIOL360 - Cell Biology (1.5) BIOL361 - Molecular Genetics and Genomics (1.5) BIOC300B - General Biochemistry II (1.5)

BIOL 404.title: Sensory Biology
BIOL 404.description: Explores the neural mechanisms underlying sensory systems: sensory receptor coding logic; signal transduction; neuronal circuitry; comparative analysis of model organisms. Related clinical disorders and therapeutic strategies are also discussed. A large emphasis is placed on the primary literature highlighting major advances in the field, aimed at building skills for designing experiments to test specific hypotheses.
BIOL 404.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: BIOL 365, BIOL 367, BIOL 409A
BIOL 404.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: BIOL365 - Animal Physiology (1.5) BIOL367 - Neurobiology: Molecules to Behaviour (1.5) BIOL409A - Neurobiology: Molecules to Behaviour (1.5)

BIOL 409B.title: Experimental Neurobiology
BIOL 409B.description: Laboratory investigations of the neural basis of behaviour. Selected sensory and motor systems studied at the cellular, neuronal circuit, and whole animal levels. Techniques include extracellular and intracellular recording and stimulation; anatomical tracing of neuronal pathways; computerized acquisition and analyses of electrophysiological data.
BIOL 409B.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOL 367
  or permission of the department.
BIOL 409B.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOL367 - Neurobiology: Molecules to Behaviour (1.5) or permission of the department.

BIOL 415C.title: Mycology
BIOL 415C.description: The diversity and ecology of fungi. Topics include: fungal molecular genetics, the role of fungi in ecosystem function, beneficial and pathogenic fungi in forests, and the importance of fungal biochemistry in industrial processes and human activities.
BIOL 415C.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOL 215, BIOL 225, BIOL 230
BIOL 415C.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BIOL215 - Principles of Ecology (1.5) BIOL225 - Principles of Cell Biology (1.5) BIOL230 - Principles of Genetics (1.5)

BIOL 418.title: Forest Ecology
BIOL 418.description: Structure and function of forest ecosystems at the tree, stand and landscape scale, including: effects of the environment upon plant abundance, distribution and diversity; nutrient, carbon and water cycles; population and community ecology; disturbance; forest conservation; climate change and global forests.
BIOL 418.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: BIOL 215
    minimum third year standing.
BIOL 418.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete all of: BIOL215 - Principles of Ecology (1.5) minimum third year standing.

BIOL 432.title: Molecular Endocrinology
BIOL 432.description: Basic and molecular aspects of endocrinology. Brain hormones and their precursors, insulin and its receptor, gene-associated peptides, new glycoprotein hormones, growth factors, steroids, the superfamily of steroid and thyroid receptors, pheromones, oncogenes, immunoendocrinology and environmental endocrinology. Lectures and presentations of scientific papers.
BIOL 432.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: BIOL 360, BIOL 365, BIOC 299, BIOC 300A, BIOC 300B

BIOL 435.title: Molecular Evolution
BIOL 435.description: Using population genetic and evolutionary principles to understand how and why genes and genomes change, and to reconstruct the evolutionary history of genes, genomes, and organisms.
BIOL 435.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BIOL 230

BIOL 436.title: Human Molecular Genetics
BIOL 436.description: Survey of the organization, structure/function, and mapping of the human genome; the biochemical and molecular basis, screening, prevention, and treatment of various human diseases, including cancer.
BIOL 436.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: BIOL 225, BIOL 230
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 361, BIOC 300A, BIOC 300B
  or permission of the department.

BIOL 438.title: Nutrient Cycling and Prokaryotes
BIOL 438.description: An introduction to prokaryotes (bacteria and archaea) and their role in nutrient cycling in forests, lakes and oceans. Diversity and evolution of populations and communities of prokaryotes and their role in the major biogeochemical cycles: carbon, nitrogen, sulfur. Genetic, biochemical, physiological and ecological aspects of processes such as nitrogen fixation and methanogenesis; design of experimental approaches to assess cycling of elements in forests, lakes and oceans by prokaryotes.
BIOL 438.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of the following:
    Complete 2 of: BIOL 215, BIOL 225, BIOL 230
    Complete all of: MICR 200A, MICR 200B
  or permission of the department.

BIOL 439.title: Molecular Epidemiology
BIOL 439.description: Basic principles and applications of molecular epidemiology in epidemiological research on infectious and chronic diseases as well as risk factors in human populations. An overview of terminology and definitions, the use of statistics, and ethical consideration.
BIOL 439.requirement_summary:

BIOL 446.title: Advanced Aquatic Ecology
BIOL 446.description: Introduction to fundamental concepts, theories and models in aquatic ecology and their application to sustainable protection and management of aquatic (freshwater and marine) ecosystems and resources. Emphasis on integrated approaches to water quality, nutrient-food web dynamics, aquatic biodiversity, fisheries productivity, and contaminant transport. Critical review of recent journal articles. Written and oral presentations required.
BIOL 446.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 215, BIOL 311, BIOL 311B, BIOL 330, EOS 311, ES 310, ES 344, GEOG 371
    minimum fourth-year standing.

BIOL 447.title: Ion Channels and Disease
BIOL 447.description: Structure and function of major voltage- and ligand-gated ion channels in neurons. Channel-related diseases and how alterations in ion channel function can contribute to nervous system disorders such as nicotine addiction and epilepsy. Mechanisms of ligand binding, gating and ion selectivity. Bioinformatic tools to analyze ion channel sequence, functional domains and structure, and electrophysiological, fluorescence and crystallography techniques to study channel structure and function. Critical discussions of the primary literature is emphasized.
BIOL 447.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: BIOL365 - Animal Physiology (1.5) BIOL367 - Neurobiology: Molecules to Behaviour (1.5)

BIOL 448.title: Neuroethology
BIOL 448.description: Examination of the neural basis of behaviour. Insights into the neuronal organization of behaviour through examination of neural solutions that have evolved in animals to solve problems encountered in their particular environments. Examples in individual species are used to illustrate how neuronal systems integrate information to shape behaviour in a real-world context. Research papers and seminar presentations based on the primary literature are emphasized.
BIOL 448.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: BIOL345 - Animal Behaviour (1.5) BIOL365 - Animal Physiology (1.5)

BIOL 449.title: Flowering Plant Diversity
BIOL 449.description: A regional and worldwide survey of flowering plants, including morphological diversity and adaptations; plant evolution and phylogeny; species concepts; modern classification and nomenclature; and experimental approaches to the study of plant diversity. Labs emphasize identification and use of keys. Lab projects include the option of a pressed plant collection. Contact instructor for details and collecting equipment.
BIOL 449.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 184, BIOL 190B
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 186, BIOL 190A
    minimum third-year standing.

BIOL 457.title: Paleoecology and Environmental Change
BIOL 457.description: Fundamental principles of paleoecology with emphasis on species, community and ecosystem responses to environmental change over the past 2 million years. Topics include: using fossil remains to infer ecological dynamics and climate change since the last glaciation; ice age megafaunal extinctions; role of paleoecology in conservation.
BIOL 457.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 215, EOS 330
    minimum third-year standing
  or permission of the department.
BIOL 457.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: BIOL215 - Principles of Ecology (1.5) EOS330 - Paleobiology (1.5) minimum third-year standing or permission of the department.

BIOL 458.title: Plant Biochemistry and Biochemical Ecology
BIOL 458.description: An introduction to plant biochemistry, plant metabolism, and the biochemical basis of plant adaptation, with emphasis on plant-specific biochemical pathways and processes, and their regulation and molecular biology. Storage carbohydrates, cell wall biosynthesis, lipid metabolism, nitrogen fixation and assimilation, and photosynthesis; biochemical ecology of secondary plant metabolites including isoprenoids, phenolics and alkaloids.
BIOL 458.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: BIOC 299, BIOC 300A, BIOC 300B
BIOL 458.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: BIOC299 - Biochemistry for Non-Majors (1.5) BIOC300A - General Biochemistry I (1.5) BIOC300B - General Biochemistry II (1.5)

BIOL 459.title: Human Microbial Diseases
BIOL 459.description: An introduction to human infectious diseases and the biology and ecology of pathogenic bacteria and viruses. Basic principles of epidemiology of infectious diseases. Methods of control: antibiotics, antivirals and vaccines. Classification, pathogenicity, molecular diagnostic, epidemiology of various types of human infectious diseases (respiratory, digestive, etc.).
BIOL 459.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 2 of: BIOL 215, BIOL 225, BIOL 230

BIOL 460.title: Honours Seminar
BIOL 460.description: Participation in seminars as arranged by the department and the Honours Coordinator. Required of all Honours students in their fourth-year of studies.

BIOL 461.title: Fisheries Ecology and Management
BIOL 461.description: An examination of the basic principles of fisheries ecology and population dynamics and how these are used as the basis for stock assessment and fisheries management. Topics include: current issues in BC, Canadian and global fisheries; growth, mortality, reproduction and recruitment; stock-recruitment and age-structured fisheries models; fisheries management tactics and strategies.
BIOL 461.requirement_summary:
Pre- or corequisites:
  Complete 1 of the following:

BIOL 462.title: Community and Ecosystem
BIOL 462.description: An examination of the development of, and approaches to, ecological research, including theoretical and empirical advances. Topics include scale, biodiversity ecosystem function, diversity stability, trophic interactions, food webs, ecological networks, macroecology, and resilience, as well as an introduction to programming and ecological modeling in R.

BIOL 465.title: The Molecular Basis of Cancer
BIOL 465.description: Clinical terminology, concepts of cancer epidemiology, DNA mutation and repair, molecular basis of cell cycle regulation, cell proliferation and apoptosis. Special emphasis on chemotherapy, gene therapy, diet and cancer, and the immunology of cancer.
BIOL 465.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: BIOL 225, BIOL 230

BIOL 466.title: Frontiers in Marine Biology
BIOL 466.description: Explores new advances in topics related to ocean biology, focussing on ocean change and responses in biological systems. Topics range from novel approaches to ocean discovery both in theory and in the field, to the role of humans in ocean change and mitigation. Content is based in ocean processes and ecological interactions ranging from microbes to ecosystem and from coasts to the deep sea.
BIOL 466.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: BIOL 311, BIOL 319, EOS 311
Pre- or corequisites:
  Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: BIOL 330, ES 344

BIOL 467.title: Neural Development
BIOL 467.description: Neural induction, patterning, cell fate determination, axon guidance, synaptic development, circuit formation, neural stem cells, adult neurogenesis. Emphasis on molecular mechanisms, analysis of primary literature.
BIOL 467.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: BIOL 309, BIOL 360, BIOL 367
BIOL 467.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: BIOL309 - Developmental Biology (1.5) BIOL360 - Cell Biology (1.5) BIOL367 - Neurobiology: Molecules to Behaviour (1.5)

BIOL 468.title: Food Web Ecology
BIOL 468.description: Characterizing food web interactions is fundamental to ecology. Provides a comprehensive introduction to the most important methods used to characterize food web interactions in terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. Topics include: isotopic ecology, ecological stoichiometry, nutritional geometry, lipid tracers and molecular tracers.
BIOL 468.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:

    minimum third-year standing.

BIOL 469.title: Introduction to Computational Genomics
BIOL 469.description: Practical introduction to computational genomics and bioinformatics. Lectures include sequencing and genomic techniques. Labs include command-line programming, data processing and visualizing in R, genome assembly, RNA-seq analysis, sequence alignment, variant calling and basic population genomics. Engagement with primary genomics literature. Analysis of genomic data as a final project.

BME 200.title: Molecular and Cellular Physiology for Engineers
BME 200.description: Examines the basic structures and processes that make up cells and tissues, including protein synthesis, cellular tissues, and control of cellular processes, using principles from engineering kinetics and transport processes. Includes wet lab exercises.

BME 320.title: Engineering Materials with BME applications
BME 320.description: Materials for engineering focused on biomaterials and biomedical applications; atomic structure for biomaterials including metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites; crystalline structures; mechanical properties of metals, ceramics, and polymers, and their application as biomaterials; properties of semiconductors; electrical & optical properties of polymers, ceramics, and metal; applications of polymers as biomaterials in tissue engineering and drug delivery systems.

BME 335.title: Biosensors and Instrumentation
BME 335.description: Principles of biomedical devices and instrumentation. Sensors and transducers (such as voltage sensors, optical sensors, displacement/pressure sensors and accelerometers, and acoustic sensors). Signal filtering and amplification (Bode plots, passive and active filters, noise in electrical circuits). Data acquisition and signal processing (sampling theory and signal aliasing, analogue-to-digital conversion). ECG. EEG. Hearing aids. Wearable and implanted devices. Instrument/device safety.

    Complete 1 of: ECE 260, ECE 265
    Complete all of: ECE 250

BME 350.description: Design methodology; recognizing and defining open-ended biomedical engineering problems, problem definition, concept generation, project planning, modelling, analysis, decision making, design synthesis, prototyping and testing. Teamwork and small group design projects. Introduction to engineering graphics; perspective and orthographic projects; 3D models, dimensioning and tolerancing; generation of engineering drawings with CAD systems.

BME 402.title: Biomedical Imaging Modalities
BME 402.description: Principles of biomedical imaging modalities with emphasis on ultrasound, x-ray, computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The theory of wave propagation, impedance matching, wave-particle duality, quantum physics and nuclear magnetic resonance for medical imaging.

BME 403.title: Medical Image Processing
BME 403.description: Image processing and understanding techniques applied in medical imaging technologies such as CT, MRI, ultrasound, X-ray. Design of computer aided diagnosis systems. Algorithms for filtering, edge detection, segmentation, registration and 3D visualization of medical data.
BME 403.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: ECE265 - Continuous-Time and Discrete-Time Signals and Systems (1.5) ECE310 - Digital Signal Processing I (1.5)

BME 404.description: Presents material in an emerging field or one not covered in regular offerings. Entrance will be restricted to third- and fourth-year students who meet the prerequisite specified for the topic to be offered. *Lab hours may vary depending on the topic.

BME 410.title: Bioprinting and 3D Printing Human Body Parts
BME 410.description: Revolutionizing available medical treatments with 3D printing and bioprinting. Collaboration between biomedical engineers, scientists and critically – clinicians. Ethical considerations and ramifications of technological advances. Includes a design project
BME 410.requirement_summary:

    Complete all of: ENGR 002

BME 420.title: Human Factors and Usability Engineering for Medical Devices
BME 420.description: Regulatory considerations for developing medical devices. Human factors associated with biomedical device design. Usability studies and clinical trials. Safety and Risk Assessment and Management in the usability engineering process to maximize safety. Design control concepts including Design History File and the Device Master Record. The life cycle of a medical device and quality management systems, device performance and the continuous improvement process. Case studies. A final design project focused on developing a medical device.
BME 420.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: BME 350, ENGR 002
BME 420.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: BME350 - Biomedical Engineering Design (2.0) ENGR002 - Work Term 2 (4.5)

BME 434.title: Biophotonics
BME 434.description: An overview of basic optics (including the principles of lasers), biology and photobiology. Practical applications are presented including bioimaging, biosensing and microarray technologies, flow cytometry, photodynamic therapy, tissue engineering (including laser surgery) and laser scissors and tweezers.
BME 434.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: ECE340 - Applied Electromagnetics and Photonics (1.5) ELEC340 - Applied Electromagnetics and Photonics (1.5)

BME 448.title: Introduction to Musculoskeletal Biomechanics
BME 448.description: Engineering analysis of musculoskeletal (MSk) systems. Basic MSk anatomy and nomenclature, effects of muscle, bone, tendons, and ligaments on MSk biomechanics. Biomechanical kinematic and force via first principles and spatial transformation methods. Technologies and methods used to assess MSk biomechanical variables. Applications of above concepts to computer assisted surgery and computational modelling.

Prerequisites:

    Complete 1 of: BME 350, MECH 350
    Complete all of: MECH 220, MECH 242

BME 452.title: Microfluidics for Biomedical and Energy Applications
BME 452.description: Transport phenomena in microscale. Fundamentals of microfabrication techniques for microfluidic devices. Flow control in microfluidic systems. Recent advances in designing microscale diagnostics and analytical systems. An overview of the applications of microfluidic systems in biology and the concept of organ-on-chip. An overview of the use of microscale technologies for energy applications.

BME 481.title: Biomaterials and Tissue Engineering
BME 481.description: Introduction to the types of biomaterials and their associated properties. Experimental characterization techniques including microscopy, detection of chemical compositions, protein adsorption and immunoreactivity. Methods for combining biomaterials with cells to engineer tissues.

CE 200.title: Introduction to Community Engagement
CE 200.description: An interdisciplinary introduction to community engagement, community-engaged learning, and related philosophical and ethical issues; introduction to skills and competencies needed to work effectively in community; participation in community-engaged learning and research projects, and the development of critical reflection techniques from social science perspectives on experiences of community engagement. Includes hands-on engagement with community partners and organizations.

CE 300.description: An interdisciplinary community service learning course combining classroom study of community organizations, civic engagement and related philosophical and ethical issues; the development of professional competencies needed to work effectively in the community; a practicum consisting of a minimum of 40 hours of voluntary work with a community organization or on a community project; and critical reflection from social science perspectives on the practicum experience.

CHEM 102.description: Introduction to thermodynamics and kinetics for chemical transformations in the environment. First and second laws of thermodynamics. Equilibria including acid base chemistry. Kinetics of one step and multiple step reactions, with an introduction to transition states and reactive intermediates. Application of these chemical concepts to the atmosphere and oceans. Laboratory builds on the experience of CHEM 101, with practice in developing routine skills. Continued emphasis is given to reporting data accurately.

CIVE 220.description: Review of bending moment and shear force diagrams for beams. Stress, strain, stress-strain relations, and factor of safety. Beam deflection, stability of columns. Energy methods. * Indicates a 1-hour laboratory taken by students on alternate weeks.

CIVE 285.description: Influence of constituent materials on the properties of fresh and hardened concrete. Concrete mix design. Impact of loads and environment on behaviour of concrete. Properties of asphalt cement and properties and design of asphalt concrete. Stresses in flexible and rigid pavements. Pavement failures. Material lifecycles. CIVE 299.title: Geomatics Engineering
CIVE 299.description: Introduction to collection, analysis and presentation of geomatic data in civil engineering including surveying, GIS and remote sensing. Fundamental concepts of horizontal and vertical angle measurement, levelling; area computation, earthworks computation, profiles and cross-sections, circular curves. Operation of field equipment used in surveying. Principles of Global Positioning Systems, data collection, map reading, scale and map projections. Principles behind geographic information systems, spatial data and analysis and basic geodesy. Remotely sensed data sources and associated errors.

CIVE 310.description: Environmental systems analysis techniques for natural and engineered systems. Sources, characteristics, transport, and effects of air and water contaminants; biological, chemical, and physical processes in water; unit operations for air and water quality control; water and wastewater treatment processes; solid waste management; environmental quality standards. Design, planning, and management of engineered environmental systems. * Indicates a 3 hour laboratory taken by students on alternate weeks.

CIVE 345.title: Fluid Mechanics
CIVE 345.description: Properties of fluids. Basic flow analysis techniques. Basic concepts: velocity field; stress; flow patterns; classification of fluid motion. Fluid statics: pressure distribution; hydrostatic forces on submerged surfaces; buoyancy and stability. Integral analysis of fluid motion: conservation of mass; momentum balance; energy balance. Dimensional analysis and similitude. Laminar and turbulent flow in pipes and pipe systems. Flow measurement.

CIVE 351.description: Topics: design of metal structures; behaviour of members and their connections; shear lag, block shear, local plate buckling, lateral torsional buckling, inelastic strength and stability. Design of tension members and cables, beams, columns, simple bolted and welded connections. Mechanical properties of wood; effects of moisture content and loading on strength and durability; engineered woods; design of connections, beams, and columns; design of buildings, bridges other wood structures. Life cycle analysis of structures. * Indicates a 3 hour laboratory taken by students on alternate weeks.

CIVE 385.description: Composition, structure and physical properties of soil and rock; groundwater flow; stress in soil; compressibility behaviour, consolidation and settlement analysis; shear strength of soils; rock failure analysis, state of stress in earth's crust, stresses and deformations in rocks, including elastic, plastic, and time-dependent behaviour; impact of geologic discontinuities on rock strength. CIVE 412.description: Engineering techniques to accelerate the sustainable design, building, operations and maintenance of infrastructure systems in Indigenous and rural communities including housing, renewable energy, electrical grids, transportation, water supply, sewage treatment, asset management, environmental assessments and telecommunications.     Complete 1 of: CIVE 250, CIVE 350
    Complete 1 of: CIVE 242, CIVE 322
CIVE 422.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: CIVE250 - Structural Analysis (1.5) CIVE350 - Structural Analysis (1.5) Complete 1 of: CIVE242 - Dynamics (1.5) CIVE322 - Dynamics (1.5)

CIVE 423.title: Composite Structures
CIVE 423.description: Project-based course builds on fundamentals of structural mechanics, steel and timber design. Design of load bearing composite elements such as: Timber-Timber Composite (TTC); Timber-Concrete Composite (TCC); and Steel-Timber Composite (STC) beams and floor plates.
CIVE 423.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: CIVE 220, CIVE 351
    Complete 1 of: CIVE 242, CIVE 322
CIVE 423.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete all of: CIVE220 - Mechanics of Solids I (1.5) CIVE351 - Design of Steel and Timber Structures (2.0) Complete 1 of: CIVE242 - Dynamics (1.5) CIVE322 - Dynamics (1.5)

CIVE 424.title: Building Science Case Studies
CIVE 424.description: Real-world case studies on building science fundamentals and the performance and behavior of building enclosures. Topics may include: heat flow and insulation; vapour diffusion control; air leakage and airflow within buildings; water control and behavior of rainscreen walls; material durability and failure mechanisms; forensic engineering; material incompatibility issues; glazing failures; roofing and waterproofing topics; building enclosure monitoring; deep energy enclosure retrofits; mass timber construction; passive house and net zero design; and embodied carbon.
CIVE 424.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: CIVE 295, CIVE 395
    Complete 1 of: CIVE 351, CIVE 352
CIVE 424.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: CIVE295 - Building Science Fundamentals (1.5) CIVE395 - Building Science Fundamentals (1.5) Complete 1 of: CIVE351 - Design of Steel and Timber Structures (2.0) CIVE352 - Reinforced Concrete Structural Design (2.0)

CIVE 425.title: Advanced Concrete Design
CIVE 425.description: Advanced analysis and design of slender concrete members for axial force and flexure. Beam analysis and design for torsion and the combined effects of shear and torsion. Special topics may include two-way slab system design, principles and methods of prestressed concrete construction, and fundamental analysis and design of prestressed concrete members.
CIVE 425.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CIVE352 - Reinforced Concrete Structural Design (2.0)

CIVE 426.title: Bridge Engineering
CIVE 426.description: Loading, analysis and design of common types of bridges according to Canadian Highway Bridge Design Code focusing on beam-type bridges: steel and reinforced/prestressed concrete bridges. Basics of seismic design, bridge health monitoring, rehabilitation and strengthening of bridges.
CIVE 426.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: CIVE 351, CIVE 352
CIVE 426.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CIVE351 - Design of Steel and Timber Structures (2.0) CIVE352 - Reinforced Concrete Structural Design (2.0)

CIVE 440.title: Hydrology and Hydraulics
CIVE 440.description: Application of continuity, energy and momentum principles to flow in open-channels and closed conduits; design of channels considering uniform flow and flow resistance, non-uniform flow and longitudinal profiles; design of channel controls and transitions; unsteady flow; theory and design of hydraulic structures. Engineering hydrology and water resource systems; estimation of design discharge; statistical analysis of extremes; impacts of climate change on the hydrologic cycle, watershed analysis, snow, runoff.
CIVE 440.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: CIVE 340, CIVE 345
CIVE 440.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CIVE340 - Sustainable Water Resources (2.0) CIVE345 - Fluid Mechanics (1.5)

CIVE 444.title: Water and Sanitation for Low Resource Contexts
CIVE 444.description: Principles of public health engineering for low-resource contexts. Appropriate technologies related to water supply/treatment and sanitation that are commonly utilized in development and humanitarian emergency contexts. Applied water and wastewater treatment to resource limited contexts. Overview of water- and excreta-related diseases, notions and techniques of water and sanitation (and related issues), introductory notions to hygiene, and an introduction to scientific literature. * Indicates a 3-hour laboratory taken by students on alternate weeks.
CIVE 444.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CIVE310 - Introduction to Environmental Engineering (1.5)

CIVE 445.title: Groundwater Hydrology
CIVE 445.description: Review of fundamental surface and subsurface hydrologic processes and equations. Aquifer geology, properties and conceptual models. Numerical modeling. Quantifying local to global groundwater resources and groundwater flow to wells. Groundwater-surface water interactions and ecohydrology. Groundwater sustainability from a multidisciplinary perspective including engineering, geoscience, policy and economics.
CIVE 445.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CIVE340 - Sustainable Water Resources (2.0)

CIVE 448.title: Drinking Water Contaminants
CIVE 448.description: Chemistry in water with a focus on metals or other contaminants, drinking water treatment technologies, toxicology, materials flow and life-cycle thinking, regulations, and an understanding of function in an industrial process.
CIVE 448.requirement_summary:
Pre- or corequisites:
  Complete 1 of the following:
    Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: CIVE 310, CHEM 324
    Permission of Department of Civil Engineering.
requirement_notes: Alternatively: Permission of Department of Civil Engineering.
CIVE 448.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of the following Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: CIVE310 - Introduction to Environmental Engineering (1.5) CHEM324 - Transition Metal Chemistry (1.5) Permission of Department of Civil Engineering .

CIVE 450.title: Green Building Design
CIVE 450.description: Design and construction concepts including site sustainability, water efficiency, energy flows, materials and resources, indoor environmental quality. Life cycle analysis methods, including estimation of material and energy flows in the construction, operation, maintenance and decommissioning of the built environment. Innovative design and integration. LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) certification criteria. * Indicates a 3 hour laboratory taken by students on alternate weeks.
CIVE 450.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CIVE210 - Sustainability in Civil Engineering (1.5)

CIVE 451.title: Sustainable Buildings: Retrofitting, Repairs, and Recycling
CIVE 451.description: Specialties of housing in remote communities integrating aspects of structural engineering, rural municipal engineering, transportation engineering while mitigating ecological footprints; major retrofit issues that consider safety, serviceability and aspects dealing with environmental factors, energy consumption and movement of moisture. Potential for recycling building materials for further use.
CIVE 451.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: CIVE 310, CIVE 351, CIVE 352, CIVE 360, CIVE 385
CIVE 451.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CIVE310 - Introduction to Environmental Engineering (1.5) CIVE351 - Design of Steel and Timber Structures (2.0) CIVE352 - Reinforced Concrete Structural Design (2.0) CIVE360 - Sustainable Transportation Systems (1.5) CIVE385 - Geotechnical Engineering (1.5)

CIVE 452.title: Engineering for Earthquakes and Extreme Events
CIVE 452.description: Basics of earthquake engineering and seismic resistant design loads; fundamentals behind seismic hazard maps contained in building codes; ground motion time-histories for engineering analysis; risk analysis; an examination of natural disasters and their effects on the society; basic probabilistic modeling and simulation techniques and their applications to natural disaster problems; hazard and risk assessments, post-disaster rapid inspection of damaged structures.
CIVE 452.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: CIVE 250, CIVE 350
    Complete all of: CIVE 385
    Complete 1 of: STAT 254, STAT 260
CIVE 452.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: CIVE250 - Structural Analysis (1.5) CIVE350 - Structural Analysis (1.5) Complete all of: CIVE385 - Geotechnical Engineering (1.5) Complete 1 of: STAT254 - Probability and Statistics for Engineers (1.5) STAT260 - Introduction to Probability and Statistics I (1.5)

CIVE 453.title: Building and District Energy Simulation
CIVE 453.description: Building simulation skills developed for: climate analysis; geometric and building envelope design; daylight and solar gains, including glazing and shading; thermal comfort and building control; heating, ventilation and air-conditioning systems; air flow and natural ventilation; renewable energy and storage technologies and district-level energy systems; parametric analysis and computational design optimization energy flows in buildings and districts, and of the integrated nature of the building design process.
CIVE 453.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: CIVE295 - Building Science Fundamentals (1.5) CIVE395 - Building Science Fundamentals (1.5)

CIVE 454.title: Sustainable Infrastructure and Non-Destructive Health Monitoring
CIVE 454.description: Case studies of sustainable construction technologies with low carbon footprint including those well suited for Indigenous and remote communities. Stay-in-place concrete forming system, rammed earth construction, hybrid absorbable landscapes and light gauge steel technology for mass construction. Disruptive non-destructive evaluation techniques including use of drones for infrastructure condition assessment.
CIVE 454.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: CIVE 200, CIVE 210, CIVE 285, CIVE 299
    Complete 1 of: CIVE 295, CIVE 395
CIVE 454.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete all of: CIVE200 - Engineering Drawing (1.5) CIVE210 - Sustainability in Civil Engineering (1.5) CIVE285 - Civil Engineering Materials (1.5) CIVE299 - Geomatics Engineering (1.5) Complete 1 of: CIVE295 - Building Science Fundamentals (1.5) CIVE395 - Building Science Fundamentals (1.5)

CIVE 456.title: Sustainability and Advanced Concrete Technology
CIVE 456.description: Microstructure of hydration products and its effect on properties of concrete. Mechanisms and interaction of chemical admixtures and industrial wastes to produce sustainable and high performance concrete. Evaluation of fresh and hardened properties of conventional and cement-based composites. Focus on specialized concretes and emerging materials not limited to fiber reinforced concrete, self-consolidating concrete, high strength composites, light weight concrete, and carbon negative concrete. *Indicates a 3-hour laboratory taken by students on alternate weeks.
CIVE 456.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: CIVE 220, MECH 220
    Complete all of: CIVE 285, CIVE 352
CIVE 456.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: CIVE220 - Mechanics of Solids I (1.5) MECH220 - Mechanics of Solids I (1.5) Complete all of: CIVE285 - Civil Engineering Materials (1.5) CIVE352 - Reinforced Concrete Structural Design (2.0)

CIVE 457.title: Behaviour and Design of Steel Structures
CIVE 457.description: Behaviour and design of trusses, frames, members and connections in steel building and bridge structures. Ultimate strength, stability, and postbuckling are emphasized in topical examples including: plate girders; composite steel/concrete girders; second-order frame behaviour; high-strength bolted and welded framing connections. Other topics include: concrete filling; fire protection and plastic analysis of hollow structural section connections. Canadian Design Standards and the Limit States Design concepts are used.
CIVE 457.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: CIVE 351
  or permission of the department.
CIVE 457.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CIVE351 - Design of Steel and Timber Structures (2.0) or permission of the department.

CIVE 458.title: Timber Structures
CIVE 458.description: Timber structures; physical and mechanical properties of wood; engineered wood products and systems; design requirements of timber structures; design of timber beams, columns, shear walls and diaphragms; connections and cross laminated timber structures.
CIVE 458.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: CIVE 285, CIVE 351
CIVE 458.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CIVE285 - Civil Engineering Materials (1.5) CIVE351 - Design of Steel and Timber Structures (2.0)

CIVE 459.title: Earthquake Engineering
CIVE 459.description: Earthquake engineering related to structural design and performance: fundamental dynamics and analysis; structural performance of lateral resisting systems; basic design concepts; code requirements; laboratory testing as used in research and development of codes; considerations for non-structural components.
CIVE 459.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: CIVE 242, CIVE 322
    Complete all of: CIVE 351, CIVE 352
CIVE 459.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: CIVE242 - Dynamics (1.5) CIVE322 - Dynamics (1.5) Complete all of: CIVE351 - Design of Steel and Timber Structures (2.0) CIVE352 - Reinforced Concrete Structural Design (2.0)

CIVE 460.title: Intelligent Transportation Systems
CIVE 460.description: Traffic safety engineering; specific planning policies or other infrastructure investments to design places and networks consistent with the goals and objectives of community planning; transportation design in remote communities including ice roads and safety issues; intelligent transportation systems; design of public transit systems, mountain highway engineering.
CIVE 460.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CIVE360 - Sustainable Transportation Systems (1.5)

CIVE 465.title: Energy Systems Decarbonization
CIVE 465.description: Energy systems concepts spanning sectors (buildings, transportation, power systems) and scales (cities, provinces, countries, the globe). Emissions and decarbonization, trade-offs, low-carbon technologies. Modelling for decision-making including: model design, workflow, scenario matrices; limitations, transparency, accuracy, breadth; data handling, optimization and visualization in python. Development and application of energy systems models.
CIVE 465.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: CSC 110, CSC 111
    Complete 1 of: CIVE 295, CIVE 395
    Complete all of: CIVE 360
CIVE 465.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: CSC110 - Fundamentals of Programming I (1.5) CSC111 - Fundamentals of Programming with Engineering Applications (1.5) Complete 1 of: CIVE295 - Building Science Fundamentals (1.5) CIVE395 - Building Science Fundamentals (1.5) Complete all of: CIVE360 - Sustainable Transportation Systems (1.5)

CIVE 467.title: Data Analysis and Building Energy
CIVE 467.description: Data analysis for buildings. Real-world cases of analyzing and interpreting building data to make informed decisions for energy retrofits. Key features of building energy data, role of building codes, optimization and machine learning models. Embodied carbon as it relates to building retrofits.

CIVE 470.title: Case Studies in Construction Management
CIVE 470.description: Current topics in the construction industry and management of projects. Includes: identification; evaluation of solutions for construction site operations; factors affecting productivity and safety; measurement of on-site performance.
CIVE 470.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: CIVE270 - Construction and Project Management (1.5) CIVE370 - Construction and Project Management (1.5)

CIVE 475.title: Life Cycle Assessment
CIVE 475.description: Evaluating environmental impacts of products/services throughout their life cycle, including material extraction, production, manufacturing, distribution, use, and end-of-life. Topics: principles of LCA; conducting an LCA; interpreting results; understanding limitations; and strategic use for enhancing sustainability. Development of decision-making and systems thinking skills for sustainability assessment through case studies, lectures, discussions, tutorials and a project-based approach with an LCA development.
CIVE 475.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CIVE210 - Sustainability in Civil Engineering (1.5)

CIVE 485.title: Foundation Engineering
CIVE 485.description: Soil Investigation Programs. Soil Classification Analyses. Failure modes and bearing capacity of shallow foundations. Vertical stress distribution below a shallow foundation. Primary consolidation settlement of shallow foundations on cohesive and non-cohesive soils. Pile foundations under vertical and lateral loads. Analytical techniques for shallow and deep foundation systems design, lope stability and retaining walls design.
CIVE 485.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: CIVE 220, MECH 220
    Complete all of: CIVE 285

CIVE 498.description: Under supervision of a faculty member, major research or design project including independent work planning, literature review and research or design activities. May involve laboratory or community-based research. Thesis and oral presentation.

CIVE 499.description: A research project and technical paper/report supervised by faculty in the Department of Civil Engineering. Prior to registration, the project objectives, methods and deliverables must be established in collaboration with supervisor(s) and approval by the Department (requires 75% or more Engineering Science or Design content).

CNPY 116.title: Communication for Personal and Professional Success
CNPY 116.description: Of interest for those who want to learn about communication strategies for professional and social relationships to support success and positive mental health. Topics include verbal and non-verbal communication, assertive communication, self-concept, conflict resolution, and behaviours that influence communication success in personal and professional relationships.

CNPY 277.title: Resilience and Coping to Promote Well-being
CNPY 277.description: Examines what it means to cope well and adapt in an increasingly stressful and complex world. Introduces a multisystems/multicultural perspective of resilience. Interconnectedness of individual and community resources are defined, explored through experiential learning methods. Focuses on sustaining wellbeing through the promotion of healthy relationships.

CNPY 414.title: Group Processes
CNPY 414.description: Analysis, theory, and research related to group processes, decision-making, and leadership in a variety of settings. Awareness and understanding of self in group contexts. Includes skills practice and development related to group membership and facilitation.

CNPY 417.title: Skills for Effective Interpersonal Communication
CNPY 417.description: Basic interpersonal communication skills for active listening, empathic understanding and communication of empathy. Includes analysis of effective interpersonal skills and skill building laboratory experience. The content and skills are transferable to a variety of settings, including counselling, education, human development, management, healthcare, psychology and recreation.

CNPY 418.title: Introduction to Theories of Counselling
CNPY 418.description: Major theoretical approaches to counselling. Includes philosophical assumptions, key concepts, the process of change and interventions. Designed for those interested in counselling, psychotherapy and helping relationships.

COM 100.title: Understanding World-Class Organizations
COM 100.description: Designed to ensure students learn all of the components of superbly-run organizations. Topics covered include understanding the organizational context, strategy, leadership, accounting and finance, employee motivation, operations, customer and market focus and what successful results look like. Case studies of organizations are used to bring the course to life.

COM 120.title: Introduction to Organizational Behaviour
COM 120.description: Introduction to behavioural concepts and tools that assist in both understanding and effectively managing behavior in sustainable teams and organizations. Motivation, personality, self-awareness, communication, interpersonal skills, teamwork, team dynamics and effective team management.

COM 200.title: Strategy and Business Fundamentals
COM 200.description: Explore you, your work and society in the context of business in Canada. Topics covered include strategy, the nature of a firm and socially responsible decision-making.

COM 201.title: Introduction to Accounting
COM 201.description: Introduces financial and managerial accounting, from external financial reporting to the analysis and use of information for internal decision-making for business professionals.

COM 202.title: Financial Accounting I
COM 202.description: Introduction to the construction and interpretation of financial statements prepared primarily for use by parties external to the issuing firm or other business entity. Emphasis on accounting policies and their underlying rationale as well as on accounting techniques.

COM 203.title: Introductory Business Topics
COM 203.description: Explores topics relevant to building and maintaining organizations.
COM 203.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: COM 100
  or permission of the School.
COM 203.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: COM100 - Understanding World-Class Organizations (1.5) or permission of the School.

COM 204.title: Introduction to Professional Practice
COM 204.description: Preparation and training to undertake Commerce co-op work terms. Includes preparation of cover letters and resumés, skills assessment and analysis, networking and interview skill development and career planning.
COM 204.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Minimum second-year standing
    admission to BCom program
  or permission of the school.
COM 204.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Minimum second-year standing admission to BCom program or permission of the school.

COM 205.title: Professional Skills Development
COM 205.description: Designed to ensure all Commerce students develop foundation, communication, personal and professional skills. The foundation skills include those necessary to complete the program of studies in the Gustavson School of Business. Other topics include presentations, public speaking, teamwork, time management, networking, business etiquette and community involvement. Students also develop methods to help establish a career mission. This is a non-credit but mandatory course for all Bachelor of Commerce students.
COM 205.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to BCom program core.

COM 206B.title: Business English and Communications - Level II
COM 206B.description: Development and enhancement of skills in written business communication, oral business communication and non-verbal communication. Students learn how to develop efficient use of verbal and non-verbal skills in business situations; how to use language to convey specific messages to intended audiences; develop and use techniques for information management. Perfection of grammar, written communication and increased vocabulary.

COM 206C.title: Business English and Communications - Level III
COM 206C.description: Development and enhancement of skills in written business communication, oral business communication and non-verbal communication. Students learn how to develop efficient use of verbal and non-verbal skills in business situations; how to use language to convey specific messages to intended audiences; develop and use techniques for information management. Concentration is on pronunciation, building vocabulary and comprehension of complex literature.

COM 220.title: Organizational Behaviour
COM 220.description: Introduction to behavioural concepts and tools that assist the manager in both understanding behaviour in organizations and improving organizational effectiveness. Topics include individual motivation, perception and communication, managerial roles, schools of management theories, group processes and team work, leadership, supervision and introduction to organizational structure, processes and culture.

COM 224.title: Organizations, Community and Society I
COM 224.description: Examines approaches to addressing people-related issues and opportunities for individuals, teams and leaders, while braiding indigenous perspectives and sustainability to enhance organizational effectiveness. Leadership, culture, job design, human resource management, emphasizing frameworks for enhancing organizational practice and understanding similarities and differences in communities and societies in the work context.
COM 224.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: COM 120
  Admission to BCom program.
Corequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Concurrently enrolled in: COM 232, COM 251, COM 292
    or permission of the school.
COM 224.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: COM120 - Introduction to Organizational Behaviour (1.5) Admission to BCom program. COM 232.title: Business Analytics
COM 232.description: Introduction to the fundamental tools and techniques in business analytics, focusing on data-driven decision-making in business environments.
COM 232.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: ECON 246, STAT 252, STAT 254, STAT 256, STAT 260
    Admission to BCom program.
Corequisites:
  Concurrently enrolled in: COM 224, COM 251, COM 292
  or permission of the school.

Concurrently enrolled in: COM224 - Organizations, Community and Society I (1.5) COM251 - Marketing in Motion Strategies for a Digital World (1.5) COM292 - Law and Ethics (1.5) or permission of the school.

COM 240.title: Management Finance
COM 240.description: An introduction to corporate financial management. Provides a framework, concepts, and tools for analyzing financial decisions. Main topics include discounted cash flow techniques, financial statement analysis, capital budgeting, valuation of stocks and bonds, tax environments, risk and return tradeoffs, diversification, capital market efficiency, and an introduction to international finance issues.

COM 247.title: Personal Financial Management
COM 247.description: Introduction to personal financial management and planning. Main topics are money and finance, banking and the financial system, salaries and income taxes, budgeting and saving, credit scores and borrowing, investing and financial advice and real estate and mortgages.

COM 250.title: Marketing in the Modern World
COM 250.description: Key marketing concepts and decisions needed to practice marketing in small and large organizations. Segmentation, positioning, marketing strategy, and marketing mix decisions such as pricing, distribution, and communication strategy. Apply concepts to make effective marketing decisions.

COM 251.title: Marketing in Motion Strategies for a Digital World
COM 251.description: Introduction to the critical variables organizations face in an evolving market landscape. Insights into customer behaviour, market segmentation, product development, management, and innovation, use of digital and social media, and the importance of these channels in today's marketing mix, strategies for effective promotion, leveraging data-driven insights to engage customers in meaningful ways.
COM 251.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: COM 100
  Admission to BCom program.
Corequisites:
  Concurrently enrolled in: COM 224, COM 232, COM 292
  or permission of the school.
COM 251.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: COM100 - Understanding World-Class Organizations (1.5) Admission to BCom program. Concurrently enrolled in: COM224 - Organizations, Community and Society I (1.5) COM232 - Business Analytics (1.5) COM292 - Law and Ethics (1.5) or permission of the school.

COM 290.title: Introduction to Canadian Business
COM 290.description: An overview of the Canadian business system. An examination of the economic, geographical, historical, legal, and political factors. Examples may include the business functions of production, marketing, finance and human resources. Emphasis on management case studies, oral presentations and working in groups.

COM 292.title: Law and Ethics
COM 292.description: Examination of aspects of law and ethics that are particularly relevant to those who own, manage or are employed by a business enterprise. Subjects include ethical frameworks, personal ethics, common law doctrines (such as contract and negligence), legislation (such as the Business Corporations Act) and other legal and ethical principles that affect business decision making in a global environment.
COM 292.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to BCom program.
Corequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Concurrently enrolled in: COM 224, COM 232, COM 251
    or permission of the school.
COM 292.prerequisite_text: Admission to BCom program. Complete all of the following Concurrently enrolled in: COM224 - Organizations, Community and Society I (1.5) COM232 - Business Analytics (1.5) COM251 - Marketing in Motion Strategies for a Digital World (1.5) or permission of the school.

COM 301.title: Finance
COM 301.description: Introduction to finance. Provides frameworks, concepts and tools for analyzing financial decisions from the fields including corporate finance, investments and international finance.

COM 302.title: Legal Environment of Business
COM 302.description: Examines a number of legal principles that affect businesses and other organizations (e.g. non-profit organizations) in our society. Topics include the law of tort, contract, business organizations and property. Focuses on specialized areas such as the law of negligence, international business transactions, employment contracts, intellectual property and fiduciary obligations.

COM 315.title: Financial Accounting
COM 315.description: Introduces concepts in a manner that prepares managers to use information presented in Balance Sheets, Income Statements, and Cash Flow statements for relevant financial decision making, reviewing of financial statements, understanding financial statement analysis.

COM 316.title: Management Accounting
COM 316.description: Introduction to the managerial accounting tools and models available to managers for use in their planning, controlling and global decision-making functions. Behaviour of costs, the differential concept, short-run choice decisions, cost-volume-profit relationships, variance analysis and the management control process.

COM 317.description: Introduces the development and use of accounting information for management planning and control and the development of cost information for financial reports.

COM 321.title: Leading People and Organizations I
COM 321.description: Examines the behaviours of individuals, groups and organizations and the issues associated with managing the employment relationship. Topics include leadership, values, motivation, recruitment and hiring, feedback, communication, conflict management and teams.

COM 322.title: Leading People and Organizations II
COM 322.description: Examines the behaviours of individuals, groups and organizations from an organizational design perspective, and the issues associated with managing the employment relationship. Topics include organizational goals, structure and growth; organizational culture; power and politics; retention practices; performance review; compensation; and selected employment and human rights legislation.

COM 331.title: Technology Management
COM 331.description: The use of computer-based information systems in achieving the information objectives of the organization. Fundamentals of hardware, software, networks, electronic commerce and business applications. Focus is on the responsible use of information systems and technology to support business strategy, operations and decision making. COM 332.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of understanding Artificial Intelligence, with a focus on how this technology intersects with and influences the world of business.

COM 341.title: Operations Management
COM 341.description: Introduction to both the broad strategic and tactical decisions of operations management. Project planning/management, process choice, process flow analysis, location and layout of facilities, capacity and resource planning, job design, inventory control, scheduling, supply chain management, quality management and quality control. The link between operations management and other functional areas of business are evaluated.

COM 351.title: Marketing Principles and Management
COM 351.description: Students learn and apply basic marketing theory, concepts and tools to make and defend key marketing decisions relating to: market segmentation, positioning, product development and management, pricing, distribution management and marketing communications. Emphasis is placed on both the fundamental principles of marketing and their application in a variety of industry and international contexts.

COM 361.title: International Business and Strategy
COM 361.description: Focuses on key aspects of doing business globally and introduces business strategy: forces of globalization; how business conditions and practices differ from country to country; free trade and protectionism; exporting, licensing, and foreign direct investment; exchange rates and the complications that arise when dealing with multiple currencies; and strategic and organizational issues for firms.

COM 362.title: Business and Sustainability
COM 362.description: Introduces the changing role of business as managers face many social, political, economic, and ecological forces. Examines how these forces pressure businesses to question existing traditional operating approaches. Introduces key concepts of corporate social responsibility, business and sustainability, sustainable development, and social entrepreneurship. Examines how firms respond to calls for more sustainable economic, social, and ecological operating approaches. Introduces concepts, tools and frameworks that assist businesses to effect transition to more sustainable practices.
COM 362.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to BCom program core.

COM 371.title: Management Finance

COM 435.description: Examines the relations of a corporation to its stakeholders - customers, stockholders, government, unions and society at large. COM 445.description: Serves as a continuation of the introductory finance course to more advanced applications of the techniques, concepts, and tools of corporate finance. Main topics include issuance of debt and equity, cost of capital, capital structure, financial leverage, working capital management, the company size-up, and valuation using market multiples of comparable companies and discounted cash flow (DCF) modelling.

COM 447.description: Hands-on experience managing a $1.2 million portfolio of stocks and bonds, in close coordination with industry and academic experts. Ethical and professional standards, ESG integration, asset allocation, equity and fixed income investments, economics and portfolio management.

COM 450.description: Content reflects the interests of the faculty members and current issues in business and industry. Topics may include non-traditional forms of work organizations, leadership, organizational development and development of managerial skills.

COM 470.title: Business Research
COM 470.description: Business research project for students participating in INTEP. While overseas on exchange, students conduct a research project on a specific business and management topic related to the country they are visiting. Projects must be planned and approved by the instructor prior to departure. Upon return, a written report is required.

COM 480.description: Conducted overseas as part of INTEP. An overseas immersion in cultural orientation, cultural sensitivity, on-site company visits with intensive foreign language training.

COM 487.title: Applied Consulting and Business Analysis
COM 487.description: How to approach and present business case analysis in an applied setting. Focuses on solving real world business problems using creative, analytical and critical thinking skills.

COM 490.title: Directed Studies in Management
COM 490.description: A specialized course which is a guided study under the supervision of a faculty member. Students interested in completing a directed studies course are responsible for selecting their topic and finding a faculty member willing to act as their supervisor. When agreement is reached between the student and faculty member, a Directed Studies Proposal, outlining the project and the paper, must be completed, signed by both the student and faculty member, and submitted to the BCom office for final approval.

COM 495.description: Effectively communicating ideas, goods, or services to internal and external audiences. Develop integrated marketing communications plan and hands on learning projects. CS 001.title: Introduction to the Place: the Geography and History of Canada
CS 001.description: This non-credit course must be taken by all students in the Program prior to 101 and 102.

CS 101.title: Introduction to Canadian Culture
CS 101.description: An introduction to the multidisciplinary study of cultural structures and expressions in Canada, including such forms as literature, the fine arts, mass media and communications.

CS 102.title: Introduction to Canadian Contemporary Issues
CS 102.description: An introduction to contemporary issues in Canadian society including politics, economic and social structures, cultural and arts policy, science and technology, multiculturalism, bilingualism, First Nations, and women's issues.

CS 200.title: Topics in Canadian Studies
CS 200.description: Topics of current interest including Canadian art, film, culture and social, political and environmental issues.

CS 201.title: Issues and Ideas in Canadian Environmentalism
CS 201.description: An exploration of the connections between Canadian culture and environment including an examination of our cultural worldview both past and present. Investigates how our sense of nation, national destiny and religious, cultural and ethnic inheritance has shaped and continues to shape our ideas of the wilderness, the Canadian environment and environmental issues.

CS 211.title: A Cultural Study of Poverty and Homelessness in Canada
CS 211.description: Explores the homelessness crisis through the lens of Canadian social policy formulation focusing on connections between past policy decisions and current problems. Evaluates policy solutions and contextualizes the Canadian experience with that of other jurisdictions. Themes include: mental illness and addiction; racial, gender and age determinants of poverty and homelessness past and present; Indigenous homelessness; neoliberalism; inequality and the politics of defining and measuring poverty.

CSC 100.title: Elementary Computing
CSC 100.description: An introduction to computing for the nonspecialist. Topics covered include the basic structure of a digital computer system; applications of computers in the home, office and industry; and implications of computers for society. Hands-on experience with a microcomputer and the use of some practical software packages are given.

CSC 103.title: Introductory Programming and Software Development
CSC 103.description: An introduction to the technical competencies in software development. Topics include an introduction to basic computing, problem solving and programming concepts including: variables, functions, objects, conditionals and loops; software development methodologies; version control systems; software tools; scripting languages; and collaboration tools and techniques. An ongoing collaborative project gives experience with building and deploying a software application.

CSC 105.title: Computers and Information Processing
CSC 105.description: An introduction to business computing. Topics include the basic structure of digital computer systems, microcomputers, word processing, spreadsheets, database systems, communications, networks and introductory programming. In the laboratory, students receive hands-on experience with microcomputers and software packages for business applications.

CSC 106.title: The Practice of Computer Science
CSC 106.description: A survey of aspects of the application of Computer Science. Topics include: algorithms; complexity and decidability; programming; hardware; software engineering; selected interdisciplinary topics; ethical and societal considerations. Optional topics include: cryptography; security; databases; human computer interaction; graphics.

CSC 110.title: Fundamentals of Programming I
CSC 110.description: Introduction to designing, implementing and understanding computer programs: an introduction to computing and problem solving; selection and iteration; arrays and collections; objects and classes; top-down design; incremental development and an introduction to testing.

CSC 111.title: Fundamentals of Programming with Engineering Applications
CSC 111.description: Fundamentals of computer programming with real-world engineering examples using an imperative programming language. Topics include variables, data types, statements, control structures, functions, parameter passing mechanisms, expressions, data structures, files, pointers, storage allocation, elementary searching and sorting, recursion, encapsulation, modularity, incremental development, testing and debugging.

      Foundations of Math 12
      Mathematics 12
      Pre-Calculus 12

CSC 115.title: Fundamentals of Programming II
CSC 115.description: Change the description to: “Definition, properties, representations and real-world applications of abstract data types. Including: design, tracing, implementation and analysis of common algorithms, software libraries, pointers, storage allocation and program traces. Introducing object-oriented programming concepts, abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, generic programming, command-line interfaces, Big-O analysis, recursion and systematic test case design and analysis.
CSC 115.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: CSC110 - Fundamentals of Programming I (1.5) CSC111 - Fundamentals of Programming with Engineering Applications (1.5)

CSC 116.title: Fundamentals of Programming with Engineering Applications II
CSC 116.description: Development of software for real-world engineering applications using both imperative and object-oriented approaches. Topics include basic algorithms and data structures, abstract data types, generic collection types, design of large programs, using and building software libraries, user interfaces, debugging techniques, software documentation.
CSC 116.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: CSC110 - Fundamentals of Programming I (1.5) CSC111 - Fundamentals of Programming with Engineering Applications (1.5)

CSC 120.title: Society, Ethics, Professionalism and Computing
CSC 120.description: Social, ethical and historical contexts for the practice of computer science and an introduction to ethical reasoning and critical analysis in the computing profession: privacy, security and civil liberties in different jurisdictions; ethics of artificial intelligence; disinformation and democracy; sustainability and the environment with information and computing technologies; inclusion, accessibility and equity in design; intellectual property; resources for understanding relevant law; professional responsibility and codes of ethics; Indigenous and global perspectives.
CSC 120.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: CSC 110, CSC 111
    Academic Writing Requirement satisfied
CSC 120.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: CSC110 - Fundamentals of Programming I (1.5) CSC111 - Fundamentals of Programming with Engineering Applications (1.5) Academic Writing Requirement satisfied

CSC 130.title: World Wide Web and Mobile Applications
CSC 130.description: An introduction to the Internet, the World Wide Web (WWW) and mobile communications technologies. Topics include: HTML; web-page design tools; development of simple mobile applications. Additional topics selected from: location-aware e-commerce; multimedia chat services; mobile social networking; software development for smartphone and tablets. Emphasis is on relating Internet technologies to the role they play enabling mobile computing.

CSC 167.title: Game Strategy, Interaction and Design
CSC 167.description: This multi-disciplinary course explores computer games and their applications through design exercises and game playing. Topics include game console architectures, entertainment media, history of academic and application-based simulations, role of artificial intelligence research, history of computer graphics, history of sound technologies, evolution of computer game design, networked games, virtual reality, and history of video and computer game industries.

CSC 225.title: Algorithms and Data Structures I
CSC 225.description: Foundations of algorithm design and analysis, including the random-access model, the concepts of time and space complexity, worst-case analysis, mathematical modeling of applied problems and proofs of correctness. Fundamental algorithm problems, including searching and sorting. Fundamental abstract data structures, including sequences, dictionaries, priority queues and graphs. Tree-based structures, including self-balancing binary search trees and heaps. Fundamental graph algorithms, including traversals, topological sorting and connectivity testing.
CSC 225.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: CSC 115, CSC 116
    Complete 1 of: ECE 242, MATH 122

CSC 226.title: Algorithms and Data Structures II
CSC 226.description: Intermediate algorithm design and analysis. Divide-and-conquer algorithm design, including advanced sorting and selection. Advanced data structures, such as weighted graphs and disjoint set forests. Dynamic programming and greedy heuristic algorithms applied to weighted graph problems. Optimization problems, including maximum flow problems on networks. Hashing schemes and the impact of randomization. Introduction to the classes P and NP and the concept of NP-completeness.
CSC 226.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: CSC 225
Pre- or corequisites:
  Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: GEOG 226, PSYC 300A, STAT 254, STAT 255, STAT 260

CSC 230.title: Introduction to Computer Architecture
CSC 230.description: The architecture of computer systems including concepts such as CPU, memory, buses, I/O, cache, instruction sets and interrupt processing. Families of processors, CISC, RISC. Memory organization and management. Computer arithmetic. Assembly language programming and its interface with a high-level language (C). An introduction to basic networking concepts.
CSC 230.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: CSC115 - Fundamentals of Programming II (1.5) CSC116 - Fundamentals of Programming with Engineering Applications II (1.5)

CSC 299.title: Undergraduate Directed Project
CSC 299.description: Under the supervision of faculty, students participate in projects that include both their particular areas of interest and other aspects of Computer Science.

CSC 305.title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
CSC 305.description: Introduction to computer graphics. Principles of raster image generation. Example of a graphics API. Graphics primitives, data structures. Coordinate systems, affine transformations and viewing of graphical objects. Introduction to rendering, such as colour, shading models, ray tracing and volume rendering techniques. Introduction to modelling, such as polygon meshes, subdivision and parametric curves and surfaces.

CSC 320.title: Foundations of Computer Science
CSC 320.description: A survey of formal models and results that form the theoretical foundations of computer science; typical topics include finite automata, Turing machines, undecidable problems, context free languages and computational complexity.
CSC 320.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: CSC 226
    Complete 1 of: CSC 120, ENGR 130

CSC 321.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
CSC 321.description: An introduction to the basic concepts and techniques of Artificial Intelligence. Topics include heuristics, searching, knowledge representation, neural networks and feature spaces.

CSC 330.title: Programming Languages
CSC 330.description: Basic concepts behind modern programming languages with an emphasis on functional programming and its contrast to other paradigms such as object-oriented programming. Inference typing, strong and dynamic typing and data types.

    Complete all of: SENG 265
    Complete 1 of: CSC 230, ECE 255

CSC 349A.title: Numerical Analysis
CSC 349A.description: An introduction to selected topics in Numerical Analysis. Typical areas covered: error analysis, roots of equations, systems of linear equations, linear programming, interpolation, numerical integration, and ordinary differential equations.

CSC 350.title: Computer Architecture
CSC 350.description: Introduces the basic building blocks of a general purpose computer with emphasis on techniques for speed and performance enhancement. Topics include: central processor organization, arithmetic algorithms, lookahead and parallelism, memory hierarchy, control unit and microprogramming, input output devices, case studies of some recent micro, mini and mainframe computers.
CSC 350.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: CSC 225, CSC 230
CSC 350.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: CSC225 - Algorithms and Data Structures I (1.5) CSC230 - Introduction to Computer Architecture (1.5)

CSC 355.title: Digital Logic and Computer Organization
CSC 355.description: Fundamentals of logic design, computer organization and hardware components of computers and embedded systems and the development of a structured design methodology. The use of ASIC and field programmable devices. An introduction to Hardware Description Languages and their implementation, finite state machines, the use of CAD algorithms and tools for system design, and the testing of digital systems. Topics include Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential circuits, memory organization, buses and arithmetic units, basic microprocessor design.
CSC 355.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: CSC 230, CENG 255, ECE 255
    Complete all of: MATH 122

CSC 360.title: Operating Systems
CSC 360.description: Interrelationships between the operating system and the architecture of computer systems. Operating system structures, concurrent programming techniques, cpu scheduling, deadlocks, memory management, file systems and protection.
CSC 360.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:

    Complete all of: CSC 225, SENG 265
    Complete 1 of: CSC 120, ENGR 130
    Complete 1 of: CSC 230, ECE 255

CSC 361.title: Computer Communications and Networks
CSC 361.description: An introduction to concepts in computer communication and networks. Topics include layered network architectures, packet switching networks, local area networks, protocol design and network security.
CSC 361.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: SENG 265
    Complete 1 of: CSC 230, CENG 255, ECE 255

CSC 370.title: Database Systems
CSC 370.description: Data entities and relationships, data modeling using Entity-Relationship diagrams, the relational model of databases, relational algebra and calculus as formal foundations for querying, query languages and query optimization, physical representation of data in secondary storage, concurrency control and recovery, security and integrity in multi-user environments, and ethical considerations related to data privacy, access control and responsible data management.
CSC 370.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: CSC 225, SENG 265
    Complete 1 of: CSC 120, ENGR 130
