ENSH 311.title: Crime and Detective Fiction
ENSH 311.description: Study of crime fiction and detective fiction. May include short stories, novels, film or other genres.

ENSH 312.title: Horror
ENSH 312.description: Study of horror, textual and visual; the evolution of horror tropes and their adaptation to anxieties about social change, shifting ideas of race and gender, technological advancement and political impotence; horror as cultural commentary. May include short stories, novels, film or other genres.

ENSH 313.title: Children's Literature
ENSH 313.description: Study of literature written for child readers (and adults who read literature to children).

ENSH 314.title: Young Adult Fiction
ENSH 314.description: Study of fiction created for young adult readers.

ENSH 315.title: Coming of Age Novels
ENSH 315.description: Study of novels depicting the shift from childhood to adulthood.

ENSH 316.title: Creative Non-Fiction
ENSH 316.description: Study of literary non-fiction (such as essays, biography, life writing, investigative journalism and memoirs).

ENSH 320.title: Special Topics in Narrative and Film
ENSH 320.description: Study of how a select number of films tell stories. Topic is announced each year.

ENSH 321.title: Special Topics in Authors on Screen
ENSH 321.description: Study of screen adaptations of a particular author’s or set of authors’ works. Topic is announced each year.

ENSH 322.title: Shakespeare on Screen
ENSH 322.description: Study of Shakespeare’s texts adapted for film and television.

ENSH 323.title: Special Topics in Media and Popular Culture
ENSH 323.description: Study of popular media and culture. May include novels, television, film, radio, music, magazines, games, comics, criticism, adaptations and more; may focus on one or more historical moments. Topic is announced each year.

ENSH 323A.title: Heavy Metal and Religion
ENSH 323A.description: Uses the example of global heavy metal subculture to introduce key conceptual and methodological elements drawn from religious studies, cultural studies and media studies. Questions the category of “religion” while showing it as a useful tool for scholarly inquiry. Considers the impact of new forms of media on religion. Studies lyrics, images, music, fashion, gender dynamics and more.

ENSH 324.title: Comics and Graphic Novels
ENSH 324.description: Study of literature that combines text and image, from comics to graphic novels.

ENSH 325.title: Games and Interactive Fiction
ENSH 325.description: Study of games and interaction in the context of fiction. Topics may include play and affect, branching narratives, worldbuilding, fandom, predictability and uncertainty and values in design.

ENSH 326.title: American Film Narrative
ENSH 326.description: A study of American film narrative. May include films from the silent era to the present day.
ENSH 326.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Academic Writing Requirement satisfied.
Corequisites:
  Rule Not Selected
ENSH 326.prerequisite_text: Academic Writing Requirement satisfied. Rule Not Selected

ENSH 327.title: Cinema and Narrative Worlds
ENSH 327.description: Examines cinema as a medium of narrative expression and imagination across different aesthetic, cultural and historical contexts. Focuses on how filmmakers use story, image and sound to explore experiences of identity, power, conflict and change. Emphasis on narrative analysis and theoretical approaches within English studies.

ENSH 328.title: Cinema, Narrative and Modernity
ENSH 328.description: Explores influential movements, styles and experiments in cinema across different periods and regions. Focuses on how filmmakers respond to political, cultural and aesthetic change through innovation in narrative, image and sound. Examines modernisms, revolutionary cinema, postcolonial film and transnational stylistic developments, with an emphasis on film movements as artistic and historical responses to modernity.

ENSH 330.title: Literature and the Bible
ENSH 330.description: Examines the relationship between the Bible and literature in English, and especially intertextual relationships between biblical and literary texts. Topics include the history of biblical translation, the Bible and popular culture, the combination of biblical and classical mythologies in the creation of Western cultural ideals, the impact of biblical interpretation on literary theory.

ENSH 331.title: Epic Imagination
ENSH 331.description: Study of epic in English or within Anglophone traditions of Britain and Ireland across multiple genres and literary periods.

ENSH 332.title: Special Topics in Literature, Home and Away
ENSH 332.description: Study of literary representations of home and away, including such issues as migration, belonging and place. Topic is announced each year.

ENSH 333.title: Trans-Atlantic Literature
ENSH 333.description: A comparative study of literatures from both sides of the Atlantic, for example British, Canadian, American, Caribbean. May be organized around a specific theme, topic or cluster of authors.

ENSH 334.title: Special Topics in Literature and Love
ENSH 334.description: Study of literary representations of love—idealized, erotic and sexual, or socially transgressive—in poetry, fiction, drama or nonfiction prose. Topic is announced each year.

ENSH 334A.title: Adultery in the Novel
ENSH 334A.description: Study of adultery in the novel focusing on the figure of the adulteress and authors' affinities with her. May include continental European texts in translation that influenced Anglo-American modernist fiction.

ENSH 335.title: Special Topics in Literature and Social Justice
ENSH 335.description: Study of literature’s representation of and/or engagement with social justice issues (such as legal and political oppression, environmental destruction, activism, race relations and gender relations). Topic is announced each year.

ENSH 340.title: Special Topics in a Major Author
ENSH 340.description: In-depth study of the works of a single major author.

ENSH 340D.title: Existence and Anxiety in Dostoevsky
ENSH 340D.description: Major works of Dostoevsky, studied against the background of his life and times.

ENSH 340K.title: Franz Kafka
ENSH 340K.description: An introduction to the writings of Franz Kafka, whose unique short stories and novels define the modern era and whose influence extends to contemporary fiction.

ENSH 340T.title: Tolstoy and the Age of Anna Karenina
ENSH 340T.description: The major works of Tolstoy, studied against the background of his life and times, with a special emphasis on the novel Anna Karenina and its many film adaptations.

ENSH 341.title: Special Topics in Theories and Methods
ENSH 341.description: Study of specific critical theories, methods and methodologies for literary studies. Topic is announced each year.

ENSH 342.title: Special Topics in a Genre, Movement or Theme
ENSH 342.description: Study of a specific genre (such as the novel, drama, poetry) or subgenre (such as illustrated fiction, periodical poetry, erotic literature), movement or theme. Topic is announced each year.

ENSH 342F.title: Faust from Marlowe to the Present
ENSH 342F.description: Faustian bargains with the devil from the 15th-century historical Faust through the plays of Marlowe and Goethe to contemporary adaptations in literature, film, music and art.

ENSH 342G.title: German Romanticism
ENSH 342G.description: An exploration of German literature, art, music and philosophy of the Romantic period (1790s-1840s).

ENSH 342N.title: Nietzsche in Fiction
ENSH 342N.description: Nietzsche as a character in literary fiction and how his ideas manifest themselves in novels from the early twentieth century to the present.

ENSH 342V.title: A Cultural History of Vampires in Literature and Film
ENSH 342V.description: A study of literary and cinematic vampires in historical context. Without focusing exclusively on German literature and film, follows the vampire myth and its various guises from classicism to postmodernism in novels and films.

ENSH 344A.title: Chaucer's The Canterbury Tales
ENSH 344A.description: Chaucer's poetry, with emphasis on The Canterbury Tales.

ENSH 344B.title: Chaucer's Dream Visions and Other Works
ENSH 344B.description: Chaucer's work apart from The Canterbury Tales , including Troilus and Criseyde and dream vision poems.

ENSH 346.title: Old English Language and Literature
ENSH 346.description: Introduction to the English language, its literature (including Beowulf) and its cultural contexts to about 1100. May be organized around a specific theme, topic or cluster of authors.

ENSH 347.title: Major Figures or Movements in Medieval Literature
ENSH 347.description: Examines the literatures, languages and cultures of medieval Britain, normally with a focus on Middle English, from the 11th through 15th centuries, covering some combination of poetry, prose and/or drama, organized around one or more major figures or movements.

ENSH 347B.title: Boccaccio's Decameron (in English)
ENSH 347B.description: Considers Boccaccio's collection of tales , The Decameron , in the context of his life as a pre-Humanist and his association with the poet Francis Petrarch; surveys interdisciplinary cultural productions inspired by the work.

ENSH 347C.title: Voices and Visions of Women in Medieval Literature
ENSH 347C.description: Examines women writers such as Margery Kempe, Julian of Norwich and Marie de France, as well as writing for and about women in the medieval period.

ENSH 347D.title: Dante's Divine Comedy (in English)
ENSH 347D.description: Examines one of the world's great poems, the Divine Comedy, through a close reading of its three books, the Inferno, the Purgatorio and the Paradiso, and the relationship of this masterpiece with courtly love, mythology, theology and medieval thought in general.

ENSH 347P.title: Petrarch's Poetry and Legacy (in English)
ENSH 347P.description: Considers the career of Francis Petrarch, his influential love poetry and letters, his literary friendships and his enduring obsession with Laura. Highlights the milieu of his work in fourteenth-century Europe. Emphasizes the lyrics of the Canzoniere but also includes Petrarch's correspondence, On Familiar Matters and Of Riper Years , reflections on his life and thought over four decades.

ENSH 348.title: Themes in Medieval Literature
ENSH 348.description: Examines the literatures, languages and cultures of medieval Britain, through to 15th century, covering some combination of poetry, prose and/or drama, organized around a specific theme or topic; materials may be taught in translation.

ENSH 349.title: Early Middle English
ENSH 349.description: Introduction to the English language, culture, and literature of the High Middle Ages (ca. 1100–1350).

ENSH 351.title: Renaissance Literature
ENSH 351.description: A study of 16th- and early 17th-century British literature with an emphasis on poetry and prose. May be organized around a specific theme, topic, or cluster of authors.

ENSH 353.title: Shakespeare's Histories and Tragedies
ENSH 353.description: A study of selected history plays and tragedies.

ENSH 354.title: Shakespeare's Comedies and Romances
ENSH 354.description: A study of selected comedies and late romances.

ENSH 355.title: Milton’s Major Works
ENSH 355.description: A study of Paradise Lost , as well as other major poems and selected prose.

ENSH 359.title: British Literature 1660-1750
ENSH 359.description: A study of Restoration and early 18th-century literature, including poetry, prose and drama. May be organized around a specific theme, topic or cluster of authors.

ENSH 360.title: British Literature 1750-1800
ENSH 360.description: A study of the literature of the later 18th century, including poetry, prose and drama. May be organized around a specific theme, topic or cluster of authors.

ENSH 364.title: 19th-Century British Fiction
ENSH 364.description: A study of Romantic and/or Victorian period fiction. May include the novel, the novella and short stories.

ENSH 365.title: Romantic Period Poetry
ENSH 365.description: A study of Romantic period poetry.

ENSH 366.title: Victorian Period Poetry
ENSH 366.description: Victorian poetry examined in relation to 19th-century theories of aesthetics and poetics, with emphasis on topics such as historiography, medievalism, imperialism, orientalism, decadence, construction of gender, the relations between the sexes, the rise of science and the decline of faith.

ENSH 369.title: 20th-Century Poetry in Britain and or Ireland
ENSH 369.description: A study of modern British or Irish poetry (or some combination). May be organized around a specific theme, topic, or cluster of authors.

ENSH 370.title: 20th-Century Drama in Britain and or Ireland
ENSH 370.description: A study of modern British or Irish drama (or some combination). May be organized around a specific theme, topic, or cluster of authors.

ENSH 371.title: 20th-Century Fiction in Britain and or Ireland
ENSH 371.description: A study of modern British or Irish fiction (or some combination). May be organized around a specific theme, topic or cluster of authors.

ENSH 372.title: Contemporary Literature in Britain and or Ireland
ENSH 372.description: A study of British or Irish literature (or some combination) from the late 20th century up to the present focused on either poetry, fiction, or drama or some combination of genres. May be organized around a specific theme, topic or cluster of authors.

ENSH 373.title: Modern Irish Literature
ENSH 373.description: Modern Irish fiction, poetry and drama from the first half of the twentieth century.

ENSH 376.title: Literature in Canada to 1900
ENSH 376.description: A study of pre-20th century Canadian literature in some combination of poetry, prose and drama. May be organized around a specific theme, topic or cluster of authors.

ENSH 377.title: 20th-Century Literature in Canada
ENSH 377.description: A study of modern Canadian literature focused on either poetry, fiction, or drama or some combination of genres. May be organized around a specific theme, topic or cluster of authors.

ENSH 378.title: Contemporary Literature in Canada
ENSH 378.description: A study of Canadian literature from the late 20th century up to the present focused on either poetry, fiction, or drama or some combination of genres. May be organized around a specific theme, topic, or cluster of authors.

ENSH 379.title: Critiquing Settler-Colonialism in Canadian Literature
ENSH 379.description: A critical study of literature by settler writers.

ENSH 380.title: Margaret Atwood
ENSH 380.description: A study of major novels and other selected writings.

ENSH 383.title: Poetry in the United States
ENSH 383.description: A study of American poetry, primarily focused on the 20th century. May be organized around a specific theme, topic, or cluster of authors.

ENSH 384.title: Literature in the United States to 1900
ENSH 384.description: A study of pre-20th century American literature in some combination of poetry, prose, and drama. May be organized around a specific theme, topic, or cluster of authors.

ENSH 385.title: Fiction in the United States 1900-1970
ENSH 385.description: A study of modern American fiction. May be organized around a specific theme, topic or cluster of authors.

ENSH 386.title: Fiction in the United States 1970-present
ENSH 386.description: A study of contemporary American fiction from the late 20th century up to the present. May be organized around a specific theme, topic or cluster of authors.

ENSH 390.title: Comparative World Literatures after 1900
ENSH 390.description: Study of literatures in English after 1900 from Southeast Asia, the Caribbean, Africa, and Australasia, among other places. May address a theme, topic, or cluster of authors; may include comparative analysis of non-Anglophone texts in translation.

ENSH 395.title: Topics in Indigenous Literatures after 1900
ENSH 395.description: A study of Indigenous literatures after 1900; may be organized around particular themes, genres or authors.

ENSH 396.title: Special Topics in Indigenous Storytelling
ENSH 396.description: Studies various Indigenous oral and written storytelling traditions and practices.

ENT 100.description: Introduces and applies fundamental knowledge of the phenomenon of innovation in for-profit, social, government, and other contexts; provides tools to aid in the recognition of innovation opportunities; introduces use of creativity techniques, design thinking, and other tools and perspectives to generate effective solutions to complex problems; provides change management tools and perspectives aimed at the successful adoption/acceptance of innovation.

ENT 340.title: Opportunity Recognition From Ideas to Validated Concepts
ENT 340.description: Provides analytic skills necessary to discover market opportunities for new business, new products (goods or services) for existing businesses and evoke change within organizations. Explores creative skills to conceptualize innovative solutions, research skills to validate the feasibility and market acceptance of the solution and communication skills to gain the key stakeholder support and advocacy needed for value impact.

ENT 341.title: Opportunity Realization Validated Concepts to Market  Strategy
ENT 341.description: Transforms validated concepts into agile but comprehensive market ready plans to make new ventures or change initiatives happen. Explores the building blocks of an entrepreneurial mindset and how to develop entrepreneurial expertise. Applied by examining a myriad of business models, innovation models and change models that form a foundation for developing a lean success-oriented go to market plan.
ENT 341.requirement_summary:
Corequisites:

    Concurrently enrolled in: ENT 340
    Or permission of the school.

ENT 400.title: Strategic Management for the Entrepreneurship Specialist
ENT 400.description: Examines entrepreneurial strategies related to new ventures and focuses on the strategic decisions and processes around bringing new products and services to the market. Uses cases and key readings to apply to venture idea organizational strategy and strategic management including the process of choosing and defining goals, formulating and implementing strategies and monitoring strategic performance.

ENT 402.title: Entrepreneurship and Small Business for the Non-Specialist
ENT 402.description: Using lean start-up methods as the foundation, aspects of new venture development are explored and practiced – opportunity recognition and quantification, customer development research, minimum viable product (MVP) design and testing, business model design, new venture marketing strategies, financing and funding, and intellectual property protection. Students select a business idea and work independently and with their team to examine and test the idea’s feasibility, culminating in development and presentation of a sound business model and launch plan.

EOS 110.title: Oceans and Atmosphere
EOS 110.description: Origin and structure of the oceans and atmosphere. Dynamic processes that drive ocean and atmosphere circulation, weather patterns and global climate change. The coastal ocean, marine ecosystems, nutrient and carbon cycles, human influences on ocean environments, marine resources and sustainability.

EOS 120.title: The Dynamic Earth
EOS 120.description: Internal and external processes that shape the Earth and its landscapes. Nature of tectonic forces, earthquakes, volcanoes, rocks and minerals, and mountain building. Processes of erosion, sediment transport and deposition and glaciation. Global water cycle and hydrological processes. Geologic record of past environmental change and its impact on life. Natural resources, natural hazards and sustainability.

EOS 130.title: Climate Change
EOS 130.description: An introduction to the fundamental physical principles governing the climate of the Earth system, and its response to anthropogenic factors. Topics include: components of the climate system, radiative energy balance, forcings and feedbacks, the carbon cycle, climate of the past, impacts of climate change, global climate model projections, and approaches to mitigation and adaptation.

EOS 170.title: Natural Hazards
EOS 170.description: An overview of natural hazards including earthquakes, volcanoes, tsunami, landslides, flooding, extreme weather, wildfires and space hazards. Particular attention is given to hazards affecting southwestern British Columbia, hazards related to climate change, and important historic natural disasters. This is an introductory-level course that does not require a science/math background.

EOS 201.title: Sedimentary Geology
EOS 201.description: The physical, chemical and biological nature of sediments at sea and on land. The process of sediment transport, deposition and diagenesis. The origin and internal stratigraphy of sedimentary basins in the context of plate tectonics. The sedimentary record as used to reconstruct past climates, geographies, and earth and ocean dynamics. The geological evolution of western Canada as deduced from its stratigraphic record.
EOS 201.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: EOS 120, EOS 205
EOS 201.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: EOS120 - The Dynamic Earth (1.5) EOS205 - Mineralogy (1.5)

EOS 202.title: Structural Geology
EOS 202.description: Geometric, kinematic and dynamic analysis of deformation structures in rock bodies at different scales, in both brittle and ductile regimes. Stress and strain in rocks and their relationship to geologic structures. Interpretation of the physical mechanisms of folding and faulting in rocks with structural data and geological maps. The origin of crustal deformation in the context of plate tectonics.
EOS 202.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: EOS120 - The Dynamic Earth (1.5)

EOS 205.title: Mineralogy
EOS 205.description: Introduction to the fundamental principles and concepts of mineralogy and optical mineralogy. A practical and systematic treatment of the common rock-forming minerals and mineral groups. Emphasis is placed on understanding the behaviour of minerals in relation to changing physical and chemical conditions in igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary environments.
EOS 205.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: EOS 120
    Complete all of: CHEM 102
EOS 205.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete all of: EOS120 - The Dynamic Earth (1.5) Complete all of: CHEM102 - Chemical Reactivity Fundamentals with Environmental Applications (1.5)

EOS 220.description: An introduction to the physical processes that determine Earth’s weather and climate. Topics include: atmospheric composition, flows of energy through the atmosphere, small-scale and large-scale winds, cloud and precipitation processes, climate change.

EOS 240.title: Geochemistry
EOS 240.description: Thermodynamic and kinetic approaches to understanding the Earth system. Application of theory to practical questions such as mineral formation, weathering, water quality, and petroleum formation. Thermodynamic and kinetic approaches are applied to the general geochemistry of the oceans, atmosphere and solid earth.

EOS 261.title: The Climate System
EOS 261.description: Introduces the processes and mechanisms through which the atmosphere, ocean, earth, and biosphere interact to control Earth’s climate. Examines interactions via the carbon cycle and climate feedbacks, giving rise to stability, gradual evolution, and rapid change in the climate system. Develops understanding of the dynamics of the climate system by examining records of past climates and climate models. Applies this understanding to anthropogenic climate change.

EOS 312.title: Introductory Chemical Oceanography
EOS 312.description: An introduction to the sources, distribution, and transformations of chemical constituents of the ocean, and their relation to biological, chemical, geological, and physical processes. Topics include: controls on average concentration of chemicals in the ocean; vertical and horizontal distributions of ocean constituents; air-sea interactions; production, export, and remineralization of organic matter; the ocean carbon cycle; human-induced changes; stable isotopes and trace elements.

EOS 313.title: Introductory Geological Oceanography
EOS 313.description: An introduction to the geological processes that shape the ocean basins, oceanic plate creation and structure, hydrothermal circulation at mid-ocean ridges, bathymetry, ocean islands, different types of ocean margins, ocean sediments, the sedimentary record of past ocean circulation, coastal geology.

EOS 314.title: Descriptive Physical Oceanography
EOS 314.description: An introduction to the geography of Earth's fluid ocean and the physics that govern it. Topics include fundamental physical variables and their distribution, air/sea interaction, water masses and their formation, large-scale ocean dynamics, equatorial and coastal physical oceanography, and interactions between physical, chemical, and biological processes in the ocean. Participation in a single-day oceanographic cruise is expected.

EOS 316.title: Igneous and Metamorphic Geology
EOS 316.description: The physical and chemical processes governing changes that rocks undergo as they equilibrate at different pressure and temperature conditions within the Earth. Melting, crystallization and sub-solidus recrystallization as a function of bulk composition. The role of different plate tectonic settings in controlling the pressure-temperature-composition conditions of formation of different igneous and metamorphic rocks.

    Complete all of: EOS 205
    Complete 1 of: EOS 240, PHYS 217, PHYS 317

EOS 321.title: Earth History
EOS 321.description: The history of the Earth-ocean-atmosphere system is recorded in the igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rock record. Investigates how the geological record is used to unravel the co-evolution of the solid Earth (e.g., tectonics and volcanism) and the ocean, atmosphere and biosphere. Focusses on the Phanerozoic Eon, as its geological record is most abundant and best understood.

EOS 325.title: Earth System Modelling
EOS 325.description: An introduction to the construction, analysis and interpretation of quantitative models of the Earth System and its components, with a particular emphasis on the use of computers in scientific problem solving. Both process models and statistical models are discussed. Topics may include simple models of the carbon cycle, seawater chemistry, mountain building, reaction kinetics, global energy balance, ecosystem dynamics, the geothermal gradient.

EOS 330.title: Paleobiology
EOS 330.description: Processes and patterns in the evolution of microscopic and macroscopic life through time: extinction, evolution and diversification as recognized from the fossil record. Major events in the history of life. The relationship of biotas to depositional systems: paleoecology, biostratigraphy and paleobiogeography. The use of statistical approaches to describe, and test hypotheses about, the fossil record. Laboratories and field trips provide illustrative fossil examples.

EOS 335.title: Isotopes in Natural Sciences
EOS 335.description: Basic principles controlling isotope distribution, including natural abundances, radiogenic decay, equilibrium and kinetic isotope effects. Applications of the principles in the fields of: Earth history - global processes and chronology; mineralization - diagenesis, catagenesis; hydrogeology and characterization of water and air masses; and biogeochemistry and biological fractionation isotopes.

EOS 340.title: Atmospheric Physics
EOS 340.description: An introduction to the study of the atmosphere as a physical system. Equations of motion, force balances, thermodynamics, phase changes of water, radiative transfer,, waves and instabilities, predictability.

EOS 350.title: Understanding the Oceans
EOS 350.description: Provides an interdisciplinary introduction to oceanography, with a focus on societally relevant issues, and use of technology to explore the ocean. Topics may include earthquakes and tsunamis, ocean pollution, deoxygenation, ocean acidification, marine conservation and climate change. Introduces community engagement and science communication in an oceanography context.

EOS 365.title: Climate and Society
EOS 365.description: A survey of the climate system and its interaction with past, present and future societies. Topics include: climate change and the onset of agriculture/domestication, climate change and the rise and fall of early civilizations, the anthropocene and global warming. The interplay between science, media, public relations and public policy is also addressed.

EOS 400.title: Advanced Field Geology
EOS 400.description: A field trip of up to two week's duration consisting of a transect of a major geological belt (usually the Canadian Cordillera, occasionally internationally). The focus varies with location, with the Cordilleran trip focusing on the tectonic interpretation of rock packages; the processes responsible for orogenesis; the role of orogens in the construction, growth, and evolution of continents; and how orogens affect and are affected by climate and the Earth system.
EOS 400.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: EOS 300, EOS 316
    permission of the school.
EOS 400.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete all of: EOS300 - Earth Science Field School (1.5) EOS316 - Igneous and Metamorphic Geology (1.5) permission of the school.

EOS 401.title: Oceanographic Field School
EOS 401.description: Methods of data acquisition, study and analysis required for solving oceanographic problems. Includes a field component held at Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre. Focus is on planning, implementing and analyzing a field data set, elucidating the biological, chemical, geological and physical dynamics of coastal waters.

EOS 403.title: Global Biogeochemical Cycles
EOS 403.description: Organic matter is studied from its formation (primary production) through its transformation and destruction during transport, depositional, and diagenetic remineralization processes. Global carbon, nitrogen, phosphorous, and sulphur cycles are discussed. Emphasis is placed on describing the fluxes of nutrients and other major compounds within and across the interface of soils, and the sedimentary and water columns.

Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: EOS 240, EOS 335
  or permission of the department.
EOS 403.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: EOS240 - Geochemistry (1.5) EOS335 - Isotopes in Natural Sciences (1.5) or permission of the department.

EOS 408.title: Marine Geology
EOS 408.description: A combined lecture and seminar course covering modern marine geological processes in a wide range of oceanic environments:, including mid-ocean ridges, mid-plate volcanoes and hot spots, coastlines, continental margins and abyssal plains. Modern methods of data collection and analysis, including the Ocean Drilling Program.

Prerequisites:

  or permission of the school.
EOS 408.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: EOS201 - Sedimentary Geology (1.5) EOS316 - Igneous and Metamorphic Geology (1.5) or permission of the school.

EOS 410.title: Global Tectonics
EOS 410.description: A study of global tectonic systems including geological, geophysical, geochemical and geographical perspectives on major tectonic environments. A wide range of examples from different continents are used. Vancouver Island is also examined.
EOS 410.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: EOS 202
  or permission of the school.
EOS 410.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: EOS202 - Structural Geology (1.5) or permission of the school.

EOS 416.title: High Temperature Petrology
EOS 416.description: The thermodynamic and kinetic principles controlling the origin and behaviour of rocks at high temperatures and pressures. Thermodynamic and kinetic relations in igneous and metamorphic systems applied to understanding the petrogenesis of magmatic and metamorphic rock suites. Applications to the geodynamic, hydrothermal and tectonic evolution of the Earth and terrestrial planets.
EOS 416.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: EOS316 - Igneous and Metamorphic Geology (1.5)

EOS 420.title: Resource Geology
EOS 420.description: A geological study of the major types of economically important metallic and nonmetallic minerals and other earth resources, basic processes of ore formation, exploration and mining techniques. The impacts of these activities on the environment are also considered.
EOS 420.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:

EOS 423.title: Advanced Sedimentology and Stratigraphy
EOS 423.description: An examination of how geologic and Earth surface processes, including tectonic, sea level and climate changes, are recorded and preserved in the stratigraphic record. Focuses on modern and ancient case studies, with topics including basin analysis, cyclostratigraphy, process sedimentology and paleo-environmental reconstruction. Labs emphasize computational skills, including introductory time-series analysis, geospatial analysis and remote sensing, and have a field component.
EOS 423.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: EOS 201
    Complete 1 of: EOS 225, EOS 325

EOS 425.title: Aqueous Chemistry in the Earth and Ocean
EOS 425.description: Controls on the concentrations of aqueous species in the hydrosphere. Principles of chemical equilibrium and kinetics are applied to the major aspects of the global hydrochemical cycle. Investigates reactions and sources and sinks of elements in oxic and anoxic aquatic systems such as rainwater, rivers, lakes, groundwater, estuaries and oceans; also the application of natural and anthropogenic tracers to geochemical problems within aquatic systems.

EOS 431.description: Observations and theories explaining the wind- and buoyancy-driven circulations of the ocean. Topics include: wind-forced currents; ocean-scale gyres; coastal circulation; conservation of dynamical tracers; mixing, potential energy and the resulting basin-scale overturning circulations; waves.

EOS 433.description: Examines the physics that determines Earth's climate and controls how climate changes. May include study of Earth’s atmosphere, ocean and cryosphere, and comparison to other Earth-like planets. Analyses climate data and examines a hierarchy of climate models, from idealised mathematical models to complex Global Climate Models.

EOS 440.description: Focuses on the occurrence and flow of groundwater, groundwater resource evaluation, as well as the role of groundwater in geologic processes, and processes that affect groundwater chemistry, within the Canadian context of management and protection of the groundwater resource.

EOS 450.title: Quaternary Geology
EOS 450.description: Methods and theory of Quaternary research, stressing the processes of interaction between the climate, cryosphere, geosphere and biosphere. EPHE 141.title: Human Anatomy
EPHE 141.description: Systematic study of human anatomy emphasizing the relationship between structure and anatomical function. Involves detailed examination of human tissues, organs, and structural components of all physiological systems (neural, muscular, skeletal, integument, cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, renal, lymphatic, endocrine, reproductive) emphasizing those involved in human movement. Mandatory system-focused weekly laboratories using human skeletons, fresh tissue dissections, computer graphics, anatomical charts, and plastinated models complement lectures to provide an understanding of the structural organization of the human body.

EPHE 142.title: Personal Health, Wellness and Potential
EPHE 142.description: An examination of lifestyle behaviours, which have the power to enhance or diminish personal potential. Current wellness models and motivational theories are reviewed and applied to wellness planning as related to personal and professional performance. Topics include physical activity and health; nutrition; stress management; substance use/abuse; environmental awareness; goal setting; and the process of decision-making.

EPHE 143.title: Multidisciplinary Foundations of Physical Activity
EPHE 143.description: Students are introduced to physical activity as applied to health, kinesiology, athletics, recreation, leisure and education, as well as the contributions made by the disciplines such as exercise and sport psychology, physical literacy, recreation, health promotion, sociology, motor behaviour, biomechanics and exercise physiology. Concepts are explored from scientific, applied and experiential perspectives. As well, key skills such as conducting literature searches and critiquing research articles are explored.

EPHE 144.title: Physical Literacy
EPHE 144.description: Introduction to the concept of physical literacy and its importance to healthy growth and development in children and youth, and the implementation in recreation, educational and sport settings.

EPHE 145.title: Optimizing Work-life Integration
EPHE 145.description: Focuses on the importance of work-life balance for job satisfaction, personal life satisfaction and health. Techniques and strategies for integrating work and personal life are discussed and students learn how to monitor and effect their work-life balance.

EPHE 155.title: Introduction to Nutrition: Concepts and Controversies
EPHE 155.description: The basics of diet planning, dietary guidelines and weight management are covered through the application and demonstration of nutritional principles and their relationship to physical activity and health. Controversial topics such as ergogenic aids, vitamin and mineral supplementation, alcohol, diets and organic foods are discussed using a balanced view of scientific evidence.

EPHE 156.title: The Science of Batman
EPHE 156.description: The extreme range of adaptability of the human body explored through the life of the Caped Crusader; examines human potential using Batman as a metaphor for the ultimate in human conditioning; evaluates the concepts of adaptation to exercise and injury from the perspective of science and exercise training; examines the multiple sciences behind exercise adaptation, musculoskeletal injury and concussion, and limitations of the human body and mind.

EPHE 160.title: Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology
EPHE 160.description: The study of the integrated functions of physiological systems with emphasis on the nervous, endocrine, muscular, cardiovascular and respiratory systems.
EPHE 160.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: EPHE141 - Human Anatomy (1.5)

EPHE 200.title: Introduction to Professional Evaluation and Reporting
EPHE 200.description: Introduces evaluation in the workplace and provides learners with the opportunity to develop professional skills such as asking and answering evaluation questions, using computer applications to collect, store, analyze, and display data, as well as create professional communications and reports. Data communication approaches include posters, Excel dashboards, and Infographics.

EPHE 201.title: Qualitative Analysis of Human Movement
EPHE 201.description: Current theories, principles and practice related to the qualitative analysis of motor skills including basic mechanical principles (stability, force, leverage, and linear and rotary motion).

EPHE 242.title: Introduction to Human Cellular Physiology
EPHE 242.description: The study of the molecular and cellular functions in humans with emphasis on homeostasis, cellular transport, protein synthesis, energy metabolism, cellular control and blood as a tissue.

EPHE 243.title: Foundations of Recreation and Leisure
EPHE 243.description: An introduction to the nature and scope of recreation; a consideration of past influences and future trends; the role of the recreational professional.

EPHE 244.title: Canadian Recreation Delivery Systems
EPHE 244.description: An overview of the development and delivery of recreational programs in Canada. Canadian federal, provincial, municipal, private and volunteer agencies are described and analyzed.

EPHE 245.title: Motor Learning
EPHE 245.description: Neural and cognitive processes underlying human skilled action and the factors that influence learning and control of these actions. Ways in which the human motor system enables the acquisition and retention of complex movement skills and implications for the design of instructional situations to support retention and optimal performance of skilled actions.

EPHE 246.title: Strategies for Active Health
EPHE 246.description: Designed specifically for physical education teachers, reviews health topics outlined in the BC Ministry of Education's IRPs for Physical Education and Health and Career Education. Topics include Quality Daily Physical Education, Active Living, Comprehensive School Health, eating disorders, stress management, nutrition, and personal and school health planning. Also focuses on student-centered learning approaches to encourage students to become active advocates for their own health.

EPHE 247.title: Introduction to Professional Practice in Kinesiology
EPHE 247.description: Introduction to professional components of a career in Kinesiology and health sciences. Post graduate Kinesiology career opportunities are explored in depth. Other topics include preparation for professional practice, technical computer and data management skills as well as program planning and evaluation.
EPHE 247.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: EPHE143 - Multidisciplinary Foundations of Physical Activity (1.5)

EPHE 252.title: Leadership Methods for Recreation and Health Education
EPHE 252.description: Theoretical and practical introduction to leadership, teaching, communication, and decision making skills in recreation/leisure services, sport and fitness. Field experience is required as part of this course.

EPHE 253.title: Program Planning
EPHE 253.description: An analysis and application of theoretical and practical approaches for developing effective recreation/leisure services, sport, fitness, wellness, and health promotion programs.

EPHE 260.title: Exercise Prescription
EPHE 260.description: Principles of fitness and the development of exercise programs to enhance health and/or performance of children, adults and special populations including athletes, the elderly and disabled; application of programs in a variety of settings; methods of evaluating physiological adaptation to exercise using laboratory and field experiences.
EPHE 260.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: EPHE 160, EPHE 241, EPHE 241B
EPHE 260.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: EPHE160 - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5) EPHE241 - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5) EPHE241B - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5)

EPHE 270.title: Foundations of Outdoor Recreation
EPHE 270.description: Introductory exploration of how leisure and educational experiences in outdoor environments are delivered and how the outdoor environments contributes to active living, health and wellness. Leadership approaches to foster environmental stewardship, participant safety, inclusiveness and enhance the quality of participants’ experiences. Exploration of Indigenous ways of knowing related to the outdoors and outdoor recreation and the interconnectedness between the natural and built environment, recreation, culture and health.

EPHE 271.title: Group Fitness
EPHE 271.description: Application of theoretical knowledge of fitness development to groups of individuals. Blends theory and practice and field experience. Design and delivery of group exercise programming, safety, how to create supportive exercise environments and strategies for addressing potential challenges in group exercise contexts.

EPHE 310.title: Physical Education for General Classroom Teachers I
EPHE 310.description: Assists generalist teachers in planning and implementing physical education programs for the elementary grades. Students develop the knowledge and pedagogical skills necessary to help children incorporate physical activity as part of a healthy lifestyle. Overall focus is on the learning of movement skills and on the developing child as a learner. Includes a variety of teaching experiences with elementary school-age children.
EPHE 310.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to BEd program in Elementary Education.
requirement_notes: Admission to BEd program in Elementary Education.
EPHE 310.prerequisite_text: Admission to BEd program in Elementary Education.

EPHE 311.title: Physical Education for General Classroom Teachers II
EPHE 311.description: Extends and refines the knowledge and pedagogical skills included in EPHE 310. Overall focus is on broadening their application to a variety of different movement categories in the elementary physical education curriculum. Students learn to create inclusive unit and yearly plans that encourage children to incorporate physical activity as part of a healthy lifestyle. Includes a variety of teaching experiences with elementary school-age children.
EPHE 311.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: EPHE 310
    admission to BEd program in Elementary Education.
requirement_notes: admission to BEd program in Elementary Education.
EPHE 311.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete all of: EPHE310 - Physical Education for General Classroom Teachers I (1.5) admission to BEd program in Elementary Education.

EPHE 312.title: Overview of Elementary or Middle School Physical Education
EPHE 312.description: Overview of the content and structure of the BC elementary or middle school physical education curriculum. Introduces basic pedagogical skills necessary to implement a quality physical education program. Focus is on the learning of movement skills and on the developing student as a learner. Includes a variety of teaching experiences with peers and elementary or middle school students.
EPHE 312.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to BEd post-degree professional program in Elementary or Middle Years Education.
requirement_notes: Admission to BEd post-degree professional program in Elementary or Middle Years Education.
EPHE 312.prerequisite_text: Admission to BEd post-degree professional program in Elementary or Middle Years Education.

EPHE 340.title: Pathology of Chronic Disease
EPHE 340.description: Examines the pathophysiology involved in selected chronic medical conditions such as cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease, metabolic disorders and cancer, as well as understand their effects on activities of daily living.
EPHE 340.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: EPHE160 - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5) EPHE241 - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5)

EPHE 341.title: Biomechanics
EPHE 341.description: Focuses on the fundamental physical and mechanical laws that control human movement and relates these laws to the techniques used in a variety of motor skills. Teaches how optimal performances in motor skills are based on the best use of these laws.
EPHE 341.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: EPHE 201
    Complete 1 of: MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 109
    Complete 1 of: PHYS 102, PHYS 102A, PHYS 110
EPHE 341.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete all of: EPHE201 - Qualitative Analysis of Human Movement (1.5) Complete 1 of: MATH100 - Calculus I (1.5) MATH102 - Calculus for Students in the Social and Biological Sciences (1.5) MATH109 - Introduction to Calculus (1.5) Complete 1 of: PHYS102 - General Physics (3.0) PHYS102A - General Physics I (1.5) PHYS110 - Introductory Physics I (1.5)

EPHE 342.title: History of Physical Activity and Sport
EPHE 342.description: Focuses on how narratives relating to physical activity and sport in the past are constructed, interpreted and give meaning to contemporary views of Canadian society and what it means to be Canadian.

EPHE 344.title: Care and Prevention of Athletic Injuries
EPHE 344.description: An introduction to general athletic training practices. Topics include safe environments, identifying risk factors associated with specific sports, legal responsibilities and documentation, developing and implementing emergency protocols for crisis procedures and basic taping and strapping techniques. May include a practical field experience.
EPHE 344.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: EPHE 241, EPHE 241B, EPHE 160
  admission to BSc program in Kinesiology
  or permission of the School
requirement_notes: admission to BSc program in Kinesiology
EPHE 344.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: EPHE241 - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5) EPHE241B - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5) EPHE160 - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5) admission to BSc program in Kinesiology or permission of the School

EPHE 345.title: Health Education for Children and Youth
EPHE 345.description: An introduction to health education as an education-driven approach to voluntary behaviour change. Examines how health education contributes to the development of individual and group strategies to improve health knowledge, attitudes, skills and behaviours. Emphasizes approaches appropriate for children and youth, including community and school health settings.

EPHE 346.title: Motor Development and Physical Maturation
EPHE 346.description: An overview of motor development and maturation from the neonate to adulthood and old age. Special attention is given to the growth and motor development characteristics of children and adolescents.

EPHE 347.title: Sport in Society
EPHE 347.description: Exploration of the historical use of sport as an expression of culture, ideology, and political philosophy. Comparison of the way in which sport is used as a means of developing national pride and international prestige. Considers how the commercialization of sport has made it a money-making vehicle for countries, cities, multi-national corporations, and television networks.

EPHE 348.title: Psychology of Physical Activity
EPHE 348.description: An examination of the psychological concepts related to human physical activity behaviour, which includes engagement in and adherence to physical activity including exercise.
EPHE 348.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: PSYC100B - Introductory Psychology II (1.5)

EPHE 350.title: Children and Youth with Special Needs in Physical Activities
EPHE 350.description: An introduction to the development, implementation, and assessment of inclusive physical activity programs for children and youth with disabilities. The course includes experiential learning.

EPHE 351.title: Community and Population Health
EPHE 351.description: Builds on students' knowledge of individual wellness and lifestyle behaviours by exploring the concepts of community and population health. Topics include: the evolution of health promotion and population health; the determinants of health; epidemiology of health behaviours; understanding and enhancing the health of children, youth, adults, seniors; principles of ecology and environmental health.

EPHE 352.title: Introduction to Physical Activity Instructional Techniques
EPHE 352.description: Methods of instruction in physical activities for school and related groups. Field experience may be required as part of this course.

EPHE 355.title: Functional Anatomy
EPHE 355.description: Explores the functional relationship of the musculoskeletal system and related neural structures with focus on functional applications. Emphasis on designing and implementing exercises to address muscle imbalances and injury prevention in healthy populations. Causes, prevention and rehabilitation of activity-related musculoskeletal disorders are examined.

EPHE 356.title: Principles of Facility Administration
EPHE 356.description: Study of the concepts and processes of management as they apply to leisure service, recreation, fitness and health facilities. Emphasis on problem-solving techniques used by administrators and managers in the planning, designing, controlling, financing, renovating and maintaining of such facilities.

EPHE 357.title: Introduction to Research
EPHE 357.description: An introduction of quantitative and qualitative research approaches to disciplinary areas in the School of Exercise Science, Physical and Health Education. Topics include methods and design, measurement issues, analysis and interpretation of literature and analytical procedures used in research.

EPHE 358.title: Management in Recreation and Health
EPHE 358.description: A review of general administrative and organizational theories with particular reference to their application in recreation and health related service agencies. Topics include: the nature of administration, structure of organizations, policy making, human resource development, change management, meetings, strategic planning and the advancement of partnerships.
EPHE 358.requirement_summary:
Pre- or corequisites:
  Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: COOP 001, RHED 001, KINE 001
EPHE 358.prerequisite_text: Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: COOP001 - Co-op Work Term (4.5) RHED001 - Co-op Work Term (4.5) KINE001 - Co-op Work Term (4.5)

EPHE 359.title: Fiscal and Legal Management in Recreation and Health
EPHE 359.description: A detailed look at the budgeting process, financial control, goal setting, risk management and legal liability in recreation and health related service agencies. Although 358 is not a prerequisite, 359 is best taken in conjunction with 358.
EPHE 359.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: COOP 001, RHED 001, KINE 001
EPHE 359.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: COOP001 - Co-op Work Term (4.5) RHED001 - Co-op Work Term (4.5) KINE001 - Co-op Work Term (4.5)

EPHE 361.title: Coaching Studies
EPHE 361.description: An in-depth study of coaching theory. Students who successfully complete the course receive the Coaching Association of Canada's Level 1 and 2 theory certification. Requires a practical coaching experience in a sport of the student's choice.

EPHE 362.title: Principles of Strength and Conditioning
EPHE 362.description: Focuses on the development of theoretical and practical knowledge of strength training and conditioning for programming over the entire healthy population from untrained individuals to elite athletes.
EPHE 362.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: EPHE 141
    Complete 1 of: EPHE 160, EPHE 241
    minimum second-year standing

EPHE 380.title: Motor Control
EPHE 380.description: An examination of the neural processes involved in the maintenance of posture, the control of movement, and issues related to understanding the cerebral organization of goal-directed movement. Includes discussion of certain movement disorders and the relationship of disturbances to stages in the sequence of information processing.
EPHE 380.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: EPHE 160, EPHE 241
    Complete all of: EPHE 245

EPHE 402.title: Professional Preparation in Recreation
EPHE 402.description: Learners integrate and consolidate their professional knowledge and skills, refine their personal and professional philosophies, strengthen and expand their knowledge of the field of recreation practice locally, nationally and globally, and learn career management skills.
EPHE 402.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  fourth-year standing in the RHED program.
requirement_notes: fourth-year standing in the RHED program.
EPHE 402.prerequisite_text: fourth-year standing in the RHED program.

EPHE 435.title: Cultural and Outdoor Physical Activities
EPHE 435.description: Provides the opportunity for students to develop an understanding and appreciation of a variety of outdoor physical activities and cultural movement forms suitable for children and youth.
EPHE 435.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to BEd program in Elementary Education
  or permission of the school.
requirement_notes: Admission to BEd program in Elementary Education
EPHE 435.prerequisite_text: Admission to BEd program in Elementary Education or permission of the school.

EPHE 436.title: Yoga and Mindfulness
EPHE 436.description: Designed to develop each participant's level of performance, ability to analyze skills and understanding of concepts within yoga and mindfulness. Students will learn breath-awareness and develop critical thinking about "wellness". Applications of yoga and mindfulness in education, recreation and kinesiology will be explored. Students will also develop an understanding of how mindfulness can impact mental wellbeing and how yoga affects the nervous and cardiorespiratory systems.

EPHE 437.title: Net Games
EPHE 437.description: Focus on analyzing the tactical concepts and skill fundamentals associated in playing a range of racket sports such as tennis, pickleball, squash and badminton.

EPHE 438.title: Outdoor Learning and Nature Connection
EPHE 438.description: Focus on the learning and leading of a range of outdoor and nature connection activities including orienteering, nature-based games, survival skills, and safety and risk management in green and blue spaces.

EPHE 439.title: Rhythmic Movement Activity
EPHE 439.description: Explore rhythmic movement activities – those activities that require us to use our bodies in coordinated ways, often in time to music. Topics include rhythmic body movement, gymnastics, drumming, dance, skipping, marching, aerobics etc. Focuses on skill development and how to lead rhythmic movement activities in future school and community settings.

EPHE 441.title: Exercise Physiology
EPHE 441.description: Physiological responses and adaptation of the human body to acute and chronic exercise.
EPHE 441.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: EPHE 160, EPHE 241
    Complete 1 of: EPHE 242
EPHE 441.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: EPHE160 - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5) EPHE241 - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5) Complete 1 of: EPHE242 - Introduction to Human Cellular Physiology (1.5)

EPHE 442.title: Exercise Management of Chronic Disease
EPHE 442.description: The role of exercise in the management of chronic medical conditions such cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease, metabolic disorders and cancer is explored. Emphasis on pre-participation health screening, pharmacotherapy, assessment and prescription for each condition discussed. Laboratory component focuses on the the practical application of assessing and prescribing safe exercise for those living with medical conditions.

Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: EPHE 340
    minimum third-year standing

EPHE 443.title: Organization and Administration of Physical Education
EPHE 443.description: Nature and function of administration; management of equipment and facilities; organization and management of programs of physical education and athletics; survey of the organization in Canadian schools.

Prerequisites:
  Admission to BEd (Secondary Curriculum) program with physical education teaching area.

EPHE 444.title: Measurement and Evaluation in Exercise Science
EPHE 444.description: Use of laboratory and field tests in the assessment of physical performance and physique. Test administration and interpretation of results.

EPHE 445.title: Developmental and Adaptive Physical Activity
EPHE 445.description: Examination of physical and recreational activities for individuals with disabilities. Methods of assessing physical performance, adapting equipment and facilities and applying programming techniques are explored.

EPHE 447.title: Advanced Professionalism in Kinesiology
EPHE 447.description: Focuses on preparation for professional practice through aspects of health professional bioethics/code of conduct, 50 hour practicum with reflective practice, charting/professional reports, evidenced-based seminar, career planning, as well as resume development.

EPHE 449.title: Parameters of Aging
EPHE 449.description: The anatomical and physiological changes associated with human aging and the relationships between hypokinetic (inactivity induced) disease, stress, and nutritional habits to aging and the merits of various intervention strategies.
EPHE 449.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: EPHE 160, EPHE 241
  or permission of the school.
EPHE 449.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: EPHE160 - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5) EPHE241 - Introduction to Human Systemic Physiology (1.5) or permission of the school.

EPHE 450.title: Musculoskeletal Pathology and Exercise Management
EPHE 450.description: Examines the pathophysiology of select musculoskeletal conditions and their effect on activities of daily living. Advanced understanding and skills in designing and implementing exercises programs to address musculoskeletal conditions. Emphasis is on integrating health status screening into safe and effective assessment and implementation of individualized exercise prescription for each condition discussed.
EPHE 450.requirement_summary:

EPHE 451.title: Leadership Issues in Fitness, Health and Wellness
EPHE 451.description: This inquiry-based learning course examines current and emergent leadership issues in the fitness, health and wellness fields. Topics include: national fitness leadership certification and registration programs in Canada and the United States, trends in fitness and lifestyle programming, alternative health and wellness programs and services and leadership and management models in the not-for-profit, public and private enterprise systems.

EPHE 452.description: Methods of teaching game activities to students in secondary schools and related groups. Field experience is required.

EPHE 454.title: Marketing for Health and Social Change
EPHE 454.description: The study and application of social marketing concepts and strategies to address the health and social change opportunities for, and challenges facing, the recreation profession and provide a synthesis for the graduating student.

EPHE 455.description: The study of nutrition in the applied context of physical activity, exercise and sport performance. EPHE 456.description: The application of ergonomic principles to industrial settings, work site job analysis, assessing biomechanical risk factors and the development of risk prevention programs. EPHE 482.description: Understanding how the neural control of movement is disrupted in neurological disorders such as stroke, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, spinal cord injury. ER 250.title: Experiential Learning in Ecological Restoration
ER 250.description: An introduction to ecological restoration issues and approaches. Application and assessment of methods in ecological restoration. Assessment typically involves a reflective journal and final paper.

ER 311.title: Principles and Concepts of Ecological Restoration
ER 311.description: An examination of how effective restoration depends on both ecological and cultural awareness, including the physical, chemical and biological characteristics of ecosystems from local to global scales; the impacts of human-induced change; the philosophical and ethical context for good restoration; the need for and significance of community involvement; the legal and policy frameworks that direct and influence restoration activities; and the importance of understanding essential ecosystem characteristics in restoration.
ER 311.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to Certificate or Diploma program in Restoration of Natural Systems
  or permission of the program.
requirement_notes: Admission to Certificate or Diploma program in Restoration of Natural Systems

ER 312A.title: Field Study in Ecological Restoration I
ER 312A.description: Introduces basic field methodologies for assessment and restoration of local sites; includes individual and group field research, and involves field surveys, observation and background study on specific ecosystem types.

Prerequisites:

ER 312B.description: An advanced field study course involving detailed site evaluation (prescription). May involve participation in a restoration project. With permission, the practicum can be undertaken at locations outside the province or internationally.

ER 313.title: Biodiversity and Conservation Biology
ER 313.description: Biological organisms and ecosystems with particular reference to mechanisms of change and human impacts on the environment. Focuses on: biodiversity (definition, assessment methods, loss, and evaluation); population biology (concepts and research methods); habitat loss; species extinction; exotic species and their impacts; and possibilities for human intervention in alleviating trends in species loss and ecosystem degradation.

ER 314.title: Ethical, Legal and Policy Aspects of Environmental Restoration
ER 314.description: Addresses the relationship of environmental values to legislative and legal systems. Includes: ethical considerations in land management; future economic benefit and ecological cost; the land ethic; policy and legal considerations in restoration; and ecorestoration in research and natural resource management programs.
ER 314.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to Certificate or Diploma program in Restoration of Natural Systems

ER 326.title: Traditional Systems of Land and Resource Management
ER 326.description: The role of traditional ecological knowledge in the understanding and documentation of the biodiversity of natural systems and their restoration. Examination of how restoration strategies can benefit from the close relationship of Indigenous Peoples to their local environments, and from their knowledge of plants and animals, their habitats and ecological interrelationships, as well as from traditional land and resource management strategies.

ER 327.title: Ecorestoration Strategies: Case Studies
ER 327.description: Examination of specific sites illustrating restoration problems and solutions. Examples include mine reclamation projects, highway and rail right-of-way stabilization, urban ravine and stream rehabilitation.
ER 327.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:

  or permission of the program.
requirement_notes: Admission to Certificate or Diploma program in Restoration of Natural Systems

ER 328.title: Forest Restoration and Sustainable Forestry
ER 328.description: Basic concepts of forest ecology and succession following natural and human disturbance. "Old Growth": definition and characteristics. Forest practices from a restoration viewpoint: the ecoforestry model. Planning and restoration strategies for hydro-riparian zones. Analysis of silvicultural prescriptions and terrain issues (slope stability, road building) from an ecological perspective.
ER 328.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to Certificate or Diploma program in Restoration of Natural Systems
  or permission of the program.
requirement_notes: Admission to Certificate or Diploma program in Restoration of Natural Systems

ER 329.title: Mining Restoration
ER 329.description: Impact of mines and mining practices on natural systems and landscapes; physical and chemical characteristics of mine sites and debris; restoration vs. reclamation; pre- and post-disturbance restoration strategies; engineering issues; revegetation and remediation of soil at mine sites; long term problems such as slope stability and acid mine drainage; legislation, policies and regulations.
ER 329.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to Certificate or Diploma program in Restoration of Natural Systems
  or permission of the program.
requirement_notes: Admission to Certificate or Diploma program in Restoration of Natural Systems

ER 331.title: Urban Restoration and Sustainable Agricultural Systems
ER 331.description: The role of restoration of natural systems in the populated landscape; structural characteristics of the landscape and its natural ecological potential; sustainable intensive human use. Planning and design, role of green space, natural corridors, recreation, soil and water conservation and restoration, ecological landscape architecture, integrated pest management, organic agriculture, urban agriculture, permaculture. British Columbia and world examples.
ER 331.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to Certificate or Diploma program in Restoration of Natural Systems
  or permission of the program.
requirement_notes: Admission to Certificate or Diploma program in Restoration of Natural Systems

ER 332.title: Selection and Propagation of Native Plants for Ecological Restoration
ER 332.description: An introduction to the principles of native plant selection and propagation to meet site-specific objectives for ecosystem restoration. Topics include native plant propagation techniques; the role of artificial propagation in ecosystem rehabilitation and restoration; criteria for species selection; scientific and ethical principles for the collection of propagation materials; site stabilization; site preparation; out-planting; and bio-engineering.
ER 332.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:

requirement_notes: Admission to Certificate or Diploma program in Restoration of Natural Systems

ER 334.title: Soil Conservation and Restoration
ER 334.description: Physical, chemical and biological characteristics of soils and their relationship to restoration. Soil fertility; importance of soil flora and fauna, especially mycorrhizae. Comparison of characteristics of undisturbed soils. Types of soil disturbance in agriculture, forestry, mining and urban environments; soil restoration strategies; planning pre- and post-disturbance.
ER 334.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:

  or permission of the program.

ER 335A.title: Restoration of Fresh Water Aquatic Systems
ER 335A.description: Theory and case studies of disturbances and restoration; character and processes of aquatic systems; types of natural aquatic systems; types of disturbance and their impact; restoration strategies for watersheds, riparian zones, streams, rivers, lakes and wetlands.

ER 335B.title: Restoration of Marine Aquatic Systems
ER 335B.description: Provides students with an understanding of marine coastal systems and their restoration potential with a focus on ecological perspectives, with particular emphasis on the British Columbia/Washington coasts. Lectures that focus on broader scale marine ecosystem impacts and restoration issues are supplemented by hands-on field exercises and research activities focusing on local issues.

ER 336.description: Provides students with skills and tools for effective communication in ecological restoration. Introduces a variety of perspectives, methods, and skills such as speaking to policy makers and granting agencies, and putting together science communication pieces.

ER 337.title: Fire Ecology
ER 337.description: Introduction to fire ecology and restoration through in-class lectures, discussions, and field work. The course will address: natural fires and their attributes; fires as an ecosystem process; fire management and regimes; fire and climate change; prescribed burns; First Nations fire management, and restoring burned sites.

ER 338.title: Special Topics in Environmental Restoration
ER 338.description: Selected topics in environmental restoration that address particular issues, industrial sectors or biogeoclimatic variation.

ER 339.title: Climate Change in Ecological Restoration
ER 339.description: Examines how climate change shapes ecological restoration through a blend of Western science and Indigenous knowledge. Access and interpret climate data, assess vulnerability and risk, and apply adaptive responses culminating in practical tools like the Resist-Accept-Direct (RAD) framework to guide action in a changing world.

ER 352.title: Non-Timber Forest Management and Sustainable Use in Major Forest Zones of BC
ER 352.description: An introduction to biogeoclimatic zones and natural disturbance regimes in BC in relation to the occurrence of important NTFP species and the ecosystems that sustain them. Topics include the impacts of current land use and resource extraction on NTFP occurrence and productivity; and the influence of disturbance classes, biogeoclimatic zones, and current ecological condition on the selection of appropriate NTFP management practices.

ES 200.title: Introduction to Environmental Studies
ES 200.description: Introduction to the symptoms and sources of environmental problems and approaches to resolving them. Global and local food systems are used as a focal lens through which to view and understand human impacts on ecosystems (e.g. climate change, biodiversity loss, deforestation) and how those impacts can be best addressed.

ES 240.title: Ecological Processes
ES 240.description: An introduction to the discipline of ecology with a focus on understanding biotic processes as they relate to contemporary environmental challenges.

ES 250.title: Experiential Learning in Ecological Restoration
ES 250.description: An introduction to ecological restoration issues and approaches. Student engages in application and assessment of methods in ecological restoration. Assessment typically involves a reflective journal and final paper.

ES 301.title: Political Ecology
ES 301.description: An introduction to the various socio-political and philosophical issues associated with the concept of a sustainable society. Emphasis is placed on the analysis of the complex relationships between social and biophysical systems. Examines how communities and environments are being impacted by the globalization of economies and cultures, technologies and ideologies, as well as responses from a variety of local, non-governmental and international agencies.
ES 301.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Earn a minimum grade of B- in each of the following: ES 200
    minimum second-year standing
  or permission of the school.
ES 301.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Earn a minimum grade of B- in each of the following: ES200 - Introduction to Environmental Studies (1.5) minimum second-year standing or permission of the school.

ES 302.title: Capitalism, Justice and Sustainability
ES 302.description: Examines how the global capitalist economy is transforming ecosystems, and how social and environmental challenges are in turn beginning to transform capitalism. Economic alternatives are examined in local and global contexts (e.g. the social economy, steady state economies and Indigenous economic practices).
ES 302.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ES200 - Introduction to Environmental Studies (1.5)

ES 303.title: Environmental Asia
ES 303.description: Explores the contemporary state of environmental justice movements across the Asia-Pacific, how “environment” has been integrated into Asian cultural fabrics, how Pacific and Asian communities mobilize for environment and livelihood and how these efforts birth new types of movements.

ES 312.title: Environmental Economics
ES 312.description: An introduction to the economic analysis of environmental problems. Topics typically include a review of externalities, an introduction to policy intervention and the measurement of environmental costs and benefits. The application of these concepts to environmental problems in developed and developing countries and at the global level.
ES 312.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: ECON 103, ECON 103C, ECON 180

ES 314.title: Philosophy and the Environment
ES 314.description: A philosophical investigation of the moral and conceptual dimensions of environmental problems. Different philosophies of the relation between humans and nature are compared.
ES 314.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Minimum third-year standing
  or permission of the school.
ES 314.prerequisite_text: Minimum third-year standing or permission of the school.

ES 320.title: Conservation Biology
ES 320.description: Diversity of organisms, functioning of ecosystems, and the consequential impact of human activities. Topics include the nature of biological diversity; extinction and its causes; habitat alteration and fragmentation; effects of exotic species; economic and ethical considerations; practical applications and analytical tools; and legal frameworks for conserving species and habitats.
ES 320.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: BIOL 186, BIOL 190A
    Complete all of: BIOL 215, BIOL 230
    Complete 1 of: STAT 255, STAT 260

ES 321.title: Ethnoecology
ES 321.description: Environmental knowledge systems of Indigenous and other local peoples are increasingly recognized as having relevance in understanding and documenting biological diversity and conservation and in undertaking ecological restoration. The different aspects of local and traditional ecological knowledge and their relationships to western academic knowledge are reviewed and the issues and requirements for applying local knowledge in environmental sustainability are explored.
ES 321.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:

    minimum second-year standing
  or permission of the school.

ES 341.title: Past, Present, and Future Ecologies
ES 341.description: Explores how ideas and practices about ecosystems and nature more generally have come to be in the early 21st century, how they are manifest in the present, and what trends will shape the future. Rapid environmental, ecological and cultural changes are forcing a reconsideration of how we understand nature and natural processes, and how to intervene responsibly in ecosystems. Themes are drawn from landscape and community ecology, systems ecology, ethnoecology, restoration ecology, and political ecology.
ES 341.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: ES 240
    Earn a minimum grade of B- in each of the following: ES 200
    minimum second-year standing
  or permission of the school.

ES 344.title: Design and Analysis for Environmental Science
ES 344.description: An introduction to experimental and statistical ecology, including principles of experimental design and sampling methods and data analysis.
ES 344.requirement_summary:

ES 345.title: Ocean History and Changing Human Relationships with the Sea
ES 345.description: From surf culture to saving the whales, dominant views of the ocean have evolved over time. Investigates values that societies have associated with the ocean over time, the origin of these values, and issues of power and exclusion from ocean spaces. Material spans the time period 14,000 BCE to present, with a focus on the development of 20th-century perspectives on ocean sustainability, such as marine mammal conservation, fisheries management and ecosystem recovery.​
ES 345.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Minimum third-year standing
  or permission of the School

ES 347.title: Ecogastronomy
ES 347.description: Examines how food decisions, from the personal to the global, influence human and planetary health. Students develop a food literacy that extends beyond simple nutrition and incorporates cultural, ecological and socio-economic dimensions. A central question examined is: what constitutes 'good' food?
ES 347.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: ES200 - Introduction to Environmental Studies (1.5)
