STAT 191.title: Topics in Introductory Statistics
STAT 191.description: Exploration of a general-interest topic in Statistics.

STAT 252.title: Statistics for Business
STAT 252.description: Descriptive statistics, probability distributions, random sampling and sampling distributions, point and interval estimation, hypothesis testing, statistical inference for comparing samples from two populations, analysis of variance, correlation analysis, simple and multiple linear regression, chi-square test, goodness of fit test, contingency table test, time series analysis. Examples are taken from business applications. Students are expected to analyze data using computer software.
STAT 252.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: MATH151 - Finite Mathematics (1.5)

STAT 254.title: Probability and Statistics for Engineers
STAT 254.description: Probability axioms, properties of probability, counting techniques, conditional probability, independence, random variables, discrete and continuous probability distributions, expectation, variance; binomial, hypergeometric, negative binomial, Poisson, uniform, normal, gamma and exponential distributions; discrete and continuous joint distributions, independent random variables, expectation of functions of random vectors, covariance, random samples and sampling distributions, central limit theorem; point and interval estimation; hypothesis testing; linear regression and correlation.
STAT 254.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Admission to BEng program.
Corequisites:
  Concurrently enrolled in: MATH 200
STAT 254.prerequisite_text: Admission to BEng program. Concurrently enrolled in: MATH200 - Calculus III (1.5)

STAT 255.title: Statistics for Life Sciences I
STAT 255.description: Descriptive statistics; probability; random variables and probability distributions; expectation; binomial, Poisson, and normal distributions; random sampling and sampling distributions; point and interval estimation; classical hypothesis testing and significance testing. Statistical examples and applications from life sciences are emphasized.
STAT 255.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  1.5 units of MATH course numbered 100 or higher.
requirement_notes: 1.5 units of MATH course numbered 100 or higher.
STAT 255.prerequisite_text: 1.5 units of MATH course numbered 100 or higher.

STAT 256.title: Statistics for Life Sciences II
STAT 256.description: Estimation and hypothesis testing; analysis of variance and the design of experiments; regression and correlation; analysis of categorical data; distribution-free procedures. Statistical examples and applications from life sciences are emphasized.
STAT 256.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: STAT 252, STAT 254, STAT 255, STAT 260
STAT 256.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: STAT252 - Statistics for Business (1.5) STAT254 - Probability and Statistics for Engineers (1.5) STAT255 - Statistics for Life Sciences I (1.5) STAT260 - Introduction to Probability and Statistics I (1.5)

STAT 260.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics I
STAT 260.description: Descriptive statistics; elementary probability theory; random variables, discrete and continuous probability distributions, expectation, joint, marginal and conditional distributions; linear functions of random variables; random sampling and sampling distributions; point and interval estimation; classical hypothesis testing and significance testing. The mathematical foundations of statistical inference are introduced and illustrated with examples from a variety of disciplines.
STAT 260.requirement_summary:
Pre- or corequisites:
  Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: MATH 101, MATH 208
STAT 260.prerequisite_text: Completed or concurrently enrolled in 1 of: MATH101 - Calculus II (1.5) MATH208 - Mathematics for Economics and Econometrics (1.5)

STAT 261.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics II
STAT 261.description: Estimation and hypothesis testing; normal sampling distribution theory; analysis of variance and the design of experiments; regression and correlation; analysis of categorical data; distribution-free procedures. The mathematical foundations of statistical inference are introduced and illustrated with examples from a variety of disciplines.
STAT 261.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: STAT 254, STAT 260
    Complete 1 of: MATH 101, MATH 208

STAT 321.title: Data Management and Presentation
STAT 321.description: Data acquisition by scraping and other means. Data storage, cleaning and wrangling. Database administration, design and queries. Presentation of data in tabular, graphical summary, and interactive formats, including special methods for spatial and multivariate data. Statistical analysis, programming, and simulation.

STAT 350.title: Mathematical Statistics I
STAT 350.description: Discrete and continuous probability models, random variables and their distributions, mathematical expectation, moment generating functions, sums of random variables, limit theory, and sampling distributions.
STAT 350.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: STAT 252, STAT 254, STAT 255, STAT 260
    Complete all of: MATH 200
STAT 350.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: STAT252 - Statistics for Business (1.5) STAT254 - Probability and Statistics for Engineers (1.5) STAT255 - Statistics for Life Sciences I (1.5) STAT260 - Introduction to Probability and Statistics I (1.5) Complete all of: MATH200 - Calculus III (1.5)

STAT 353.title: Applied Regression Analysis
STAT 353.description: An outline of linear regression theory with applications; multiple linear regression, polynomial regression, model adequacy checking, variable transformation, variable selection, indicator variable, diagnostics for leverage and influential observations, multicollinearity problem, model selection, stepwise regression, prediction and inference
STAT 353.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: STAT 256, STAT 261
    Complete 1 of: MATH 110, MATH 211
  or permission of the department.

STAT 354.title: Sampling Techniques
STAT 354.description: Principal steps in planning and conducting a sample survey. Sampling techniques including stratification, systematic sampling and multistage sampling. Practical survey designs with illustrations. Nonsampling errors.
STAT 354.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: STAT 256, STAT 261, STAT 355, STAT 359
  or permission of the department.
STAT 354.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: STAT256 - Statistics for Life Sciences II (1.5) STAT261 - Introduction to Probability and Statistics II (1.5) STAT355 - Statistical Methods in Health Sciences (1.5) STAT359 - Data Analysis (1.5) or permission of the department.

STAT 355.title: Statistical Methods in Health Sciences
STAT 355.description: Rates and comparison of rates: case-control studies; odds ratios; regression models; Poisson and logistic regression; dose-response models; Cox's regression analysis.

STAT 359.title: Data Analysis
STAT 359.description: An introductory data analysis course for students who have had an introduction to descriptive statistics, probability distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing and confidence intervals. Emphasis is placed on proper use of computer software, interpretation of output and assumptions required for use of each statistical method. Topics may include: linear and nonlinear regression, time series analysis, analysis of variance, design of experiments, generalized linear models, repeated measures analysis, survival analysis, methods for multivariate data, and nonparametric methods.
STAT 359.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of: STAT 252, STAT 254, STAT 255, STAT 260, ECON 245, GEOG 226, PSYC 300A, SOCI 371A
  or permission of the department.
STAT 359.prerequisite_text: Complete 1 of: STAT252 - Statistics for Business (1.5) STAT254 - Probability and Statistics for Engineers (1.5) STAT255 - Statistics for Life Sciences I (1.5) STAT260 - Introduction to Probability and Statistics I (1.5) ECON245 - Descriptive Statistics and Probability (1.5) GEOG226 - Quantitative Methods in Geography (1.5) PSYC300A - Statistical Methods in Psychology (1.5) SOCI371A - Statistical Analysis in Sociology: I (1.5) or permission of the department.

STAT 450.title: Mathematical Statistics II
STAT 450.description: Brief introduction to decision theory, point and interval estimation, hypothesis testing; regression and correlation, analysis of variance. Emphasis on the mathematics of statistics.
STAT 450.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: STAT 256, STAT 261
    Complete all of: STAT 350
STAT 450.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: STAT256 - Statistics for Life Sciences II (1.5) STAT261 - Introduction to Probability and Statistics II (1.5) Complete all of: STAT350 - Mathematical Statistics I (1.5)

STAT 453.title: The Design and Analysis of Experiments
STAT 453.description: An introduction to the principles of experimental design and the techniques of analysis of variance. A discussion of experimental error, randomization, replication, and local control. Analysis of variance is developed for single factor and multifactor experiments. The use of concomitant observations. Multiple comparisons and orthogonal contrasts.
STAT 453.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: STAT 251, STAT 256, STAT 261
    Complete all of: STAT 353
  or permission of the department.
STAT 453.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: STAT251 - Introduction to Statistics: II (1.5) STAT256 - Statistics for Life Sciences II (1.5) STAT261 - Introduction to Probability and Statistics II (1.5) Complete all of: STAT353 - Applied Regression Analysis (1.5) or permission of the department.

STAT 454.title: Topics in Applied Statistics
STAT 454.description: Possible topics include: Bayesian statistics, bioinformatics, biostatistics, clustering methods, longitudinal data analysis, mixture models, robust statistics, spatial statistics, sampling theory and methods, statistics for imaging, and statistical computing. Information on the topics available in any given year may be obtained from the department.

STAT 455.title: Distribution-Free Statistics
STAT 455.description: Tests based on the binomial distribution; contingency tables; methods based on ranks; statistics of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov type; resampling methods; empirical likelihood methods.
STAT 455.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete 1 of: STAT 256, STAT 261
    Complete all of: STAT 350
STAT 455.prerequisite_text: Complete all of the following Complete 1 of: STAT256 - Statistics for Life Sciences II (1.5) STAT261 - Introduction to Probability and Statistics II (1.5) Complete all of: STAT350 - Mathematical Statistics I (1.5)

STAT 456.title: Multivariate Analysis
STAT 456.description: Multivariate normal distribution; multivariate analysis of variance; regression; discriminant analysis; classification analysis; principal component analysis; cluster analysis; and factor analysis.
STAT 456.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: STAT 350, STAT 353
STAT 456.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: STAT350 - Mathematical Statistics I (1.5) STAT353 - Applied Regression Analysis (1.5)

STAT 457.title: Time Series Analysis
STAT 457.description: Stationary time series; Box-Jenkins methodology; autoregressive, moving-average and ARIMA models; smoothing; time series regression; spectral analysis and linear filters.
STAT 457.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete 1 of the following:
    Complete all of: ECON 366, STAT 350
    Complete all of: STAT 350, STAT 353
review_reasons: "Complete 1 of the following" contains alternatives that each need several courses; needs manual review

STAT 458.title: Generalized Linear Models
STAT 458.description: Nonlinear regression models; logit and probit models for binomial responses; log-linear models for counts; quasi-likelihoods and generalized estimating equations for non-normal data.
STAT 458.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: STAT 350, STAT 353
STAT 458.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: STAT350 - Mathematical Statistics I (1.5) STAT353 - Applied Regression Analysis (1.5)

STAT 459.title: Survival Analysis
STAT 459.description: Analysis of time-to-failure data; censoring; survival, hazard rate and mean residual life functions; nonparametric estimation and comparisons of survival functions; covariates; parametric models; semi-parametric (Cox) regression model; time-dependent covariates.
STAT 459.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: STAT 350, STAT 353
STAT 459.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: STAT350 - Mathematical Statistics I (1.5) STAT353 - Applied Regression Analysis (1.5)

STAT 460.title: Bayesian Statistics
STAT 460.description: Bayesian modelling, prior distributions; Jeffreys prior, posterior distributions, single and multi-parameter models; Bayesian point and interval estimation; Bayes factors and point null hypothesis testing; Bayesian computation; decision theory. Other topics may include: hierarchical modeling, Bayesian model selection.
STAT 460.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: STAT 350
  or permission of the department.
STAT 460.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: STAT350 - Mathematical Statistics I (1.5) or permission of the department.

STAT 464.title: Statistical Computing
STAT 464.description: Computer representation of numbers, univariate optimization, multivariate optimization, combinatorial optimization, genetic algorithms, EM algorithm, random number generation, numerical integration, simulation and Monte Carlo integration, Gibbs sampling, Metropolis-Hastings algorithm; bootstrapping. Other topics may include: permutation tests,smoothing, reversible jump MCMC, importance sampling, hybrid Gibbs sampling.
STAT 464.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of the following:
    Complete all of: MATH 211
    Complete 1 of: STAT 261, STAT 359
    Earn a minimum grade of C+ in each of the following: STAT 350
    or permission of the department.

STAT 465.title: Statistical Methods for Genomic Data
STAT 465.description: Introduction to genomic data and statistical methodology for its analysis; examples of data may include single-nucleotide polymorphisms or gene expression levels, generated from microarrays or next-generation sequencing. Statistical techniques may include data preprocessing, filtering, normalization, exploratory methods, visualization, dimension reduction, differential expression, generalized linear models, corrections for multiple comparisons, clustering, gene ontology analyses, genome-wide association studies.
STAT 465.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: STAT 350, STAT 353
  or permission of the department.
STAT 465.prerequisite_text: Complete all of: STAT350 - Mathematical Statistics I (1.5) STAT353 - Applied Regression Analysis (1.5) or permission of the department.

STAT 466.title: Robust Statistics
STAT 466.description: Influence function and breakdown point; efficiency and robustness; robust location and scale estimation; robust regression; robust covariance matrix estimation; robust k-means clustering; robust principal component analysis; outlier detection.
STAT 466.requirement_summary:
Prerequisites:
  Complete all of: STAT 350, STAT 353
  or permission of the department.

STAT 469.title: Machine Learning
STAT 469.description: An introduction to machine learning methods including: Supervised learning methods (linear regression models, elastic net, LDA, QDA, KNN, decision tree, random forest, splines, GAM, and multi-task predictions); Unsupervised learning methods in dimension reduction (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP) and in clustering (K-means, clustering, mixture models); and Ensemble learning methods (bagging, boosting, stacking).

STAT 498.title: Seminar and Independent Project
STAT 498.description: Seminar and research project in statistics under the direction of a faculty member. The student is required to pursue an independent project, to prepare a written report, and to give a talk in the statistics seminar describing the work. Only available in areas of faculty interest.

TCA 210.title: Introduction to the Human Dimensions of Climate Change
TCA 210.description: Examines a range of understandings of and approaches to addressing climate change, exploring: the kind of problem(s) it poses; the toolkits we need to develop to engage it effectively; how to collaborate across diverse understandings of and priorities in relation to it, and the scales and kinds of actions that should be prioritized.

TCA 310.title: Transformative Change
TCA 310.description: Explores the limitations of conventional approaches to sustainability and considers what transformational—as opposed to incremental—change might require. Emphasis is placed on critical analysis and the skills required for decision-making under conditions of uncertainty, including planning for diverse goals, with incomplete information and sometimes contradictory forms of knowledge. Includes a focus on arts and humanities-based approaches to transformation.

TCA 320.title: Politics, Policies and Planning for Climate Action
TCA 320.description: British Columbia is used as a case study to introduce the policy and political contexts that shape climate action across scales from local to global, including relevant institutional and governance innovations. Emphasis placed on skills and strategies for engaging and overcoming stagnation and polarization; developing strategies that are responsive to climate science as well as social and ecological impacts and effective communication.

TCA 405.title: Allyship, Solidarity and Transforming Relations
TCA 405.description: Focuses on theory and practices necessary to build alliances powerful enough to transform systems. Investigates how settler colonialism and capitalism have damaged relationships with land and with each other. Explores unlearning white supremacy, hierarchy and dominance and learning to build trust, reciprocity and accountability in service of forging strong alliances towards climate justice.

TCA 410.title: Indigenous-Led Climate Action
TCA 410.description: Explores Indigenous understandings of and responses to climate change, with a particular emphasis on developing skills for respectful and effective collaboration in support of Indigenous priorities.

TCA 415.title: Adaptation Planning and the Built Environment
TCA 415.description: Focuses on skills and strategies for urban and regional planning in the context of a rapidly-changing climate, including appropriate use of downscaled climate models to guide adaptation planning.

TCA 420.title: Water Futures and Collaborative Responses to Climate Impacts
TCA 420.description: Explores the evolution of governance to address the impacts of climate change on freshwater regimes, including cycles of drought, fire and floods with a particular emphasis on collaborative governance.

TCA 425.title: Organizing for Transformative Change
TCA 425.description: Focuses on concepts, skills and practices for organizing transformational change, including strategic landscape analysis, effective communications and alliance-building strategies, and navigating cultural and institutional impediments to change.

TCA 430.title: Future Ecosystems and Communities
TCA 430.description: Focuses on the interface between communities and the ecosystems that support them, developing skills and approaches for designing mitigation and adaptation strategies that support mutual flourishing, including adaptive management, ecological restoration and nature-based solutions.

TCA 480.title: Special Topics in Transformative Climate Action
TCA 480.description: Presents selected topics in an emerging field related to transformative climate action or one not covered in regular offerings.

TCA 490.title: Practicum in Transformative Climate Action
TCA 490.description: An opportunity to apply evolving of transformative climate action skills to field-based practice through placement with an organization, community group, or service. Involves a minimum of 100 hours of professional practice activity.

WRIT 307.title: Basic Forms and Techniques in Poetry
WRIT 307.description: A lecture course surveying the functions of specific poetic techniques in a representative group of poems. Aspects of poetics discussed include prosody, sound patterns, diction and figurative language.

WRIT 308.title: Non-Traditional and Experimental Forms and Techniques in Poetry
WRIT 308.description: A lecture and discussion course surveying forms and techniques in non-traditional and experimental structures in poetry. Topics include world poetry and various historical and emerging avant gardes.

WRIT 309.title: Basic Forms and Techniques in Short Fiction
WRIT 309.description: A lecture course surveying the structural composition and the function of technique in a representative group of narrative prose works. Aspects of narrative discussed include: theme, point of view, scenic structure, role of narrator, metaphor, diction, plot and dialogue.

WRIT 310.title: Basic Forms and Techniques in the Novel
WRIT 310.description: A lecture course surveying the structural composition and the function of techniques in a representative group of novels and novellas. Emphasis is placed upon form and voice, as well as upon their relationship with such other elements of narrative as plot, character development, scene development and theme.

WRIT 311.title: Structure in Stage Drama
WRIT 311.description: A lecture course surveying the structural characteristics of stage drama.

WRIT 312.title: Structure in Cinema and Television Drama
WRIT 312.description: A lecture course surveying the structural characteristics of screen drama, making use of published film and television scripts, and of actual films.

WRIT 313.title: Recurrent Themes
WRIT 313.description: A lecture course surveying recurrent themes in film and/or English literature and in other literatures in translation.

WRIT 314.title: Changing Perspectives
WRIT 314.description: A lecture course surveying the different ways in which writers have tackled similar subject matter, taking its material from film scripts and/or English literature and other literature in translation.
